Before that pass it *could not run at all* — `next lint` with no ESLint installed opened its interactive *"How would you like to configure ESLint?"* prompt and exited 1 with no TTY — which is why CI's lint job failed at the step *before* typecheck. It no longer does; see the section at the end for what was fixed and what is left as warnings.
- **`css: true` in `vitest.config.ts` is load-bearing for one file, and finding that out cost a round.** Vitest replaces every CSS import with an empty string, so `import css from "../app/globals.css?raw"` — Vite's own way to get a file's source bytes — **returns `""` by default**, and the contract test above silently asserted nothing while passing. With `css: true` the same import returns the real source (**15,093 characters** after the theme pass; it was 8,944 before). The measured symptom to recognise: `parse(css)` finding **0 rules** and the invariant passing vacuously. It does not slow the suite (only that one file imports CSS, and `?raw` skips PostCSS). It reads through `?raw` and a `/// <reference types="vite/client" />` rather than `readFileSync`: that was originally forced by the absent `@types/node` (now present — see **Zero type errors, and a real lint gate** below), and is left as it is because `?raw` is the smaller unit and the source is not a test fixture.
- **`jsdom` is a devDependency, and files opt into it one at a time** with `// @vitest-environment jsdom` at the top; the default environment stays `node`, because most of this suite is a predicate or a truth table and jsdom costs seconds per file to boot (measured: ~6.4s of environment setup, once, shared across the jsdom files in a run). **Eight test files ask for it**: `src/components/ui/icon-button.test.tsx`, `src/components/ui/media.test.tsx`, `src/components/layout/theme-menu-items.test.tsx`, `src/components/layout/mobile-nav-theme.test.tsx`, `src/components/pages/page-view.test.tsx`, `src/test/a11y.test.ts`, `src/test/rendered-a11y.test.tsx` and `src/components/providers/theme-sync.test.tsx`. It needs no config — vitest resolves the environment from the installed package — and nothing app-side changed, so the built app is unaffected.
- **What that environment needs shimmed.** `src/test/setup.ts` carries it all behind a `typeof window !== "undefined"` guard, so the node tests are never handed globals they cannot use: `IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT` (React's `act()` warns without it); a `ResizeObserver` stub (jsdom implements none, and Radix measures the trigger it positions a tooltip against with one — without the stub, opening a tooltip throws before any assertion runs); `Element.prototype.scrollIntoView` and `window.matchMedia` (jsdom lays nothing out, and the messages page scrolls its list while the cover studio honours reduced motion); an in-memory `localStorage` (this jsdom has none, and reaching for the missing one prints Node's own `--localstorage-file` warning — see the accent section for why it is *defined* rather than tested for); and `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext` pinned to `null`, because jsdom's version logs "Not implemented" into the one output read carefully — the audit's. And `src/test/render.tsx` is a ~60-line helper rather than a Testing Library: `mount()` renders through `react-dom/client` inside `act`, and returns `byName(name)`, `settle()`, `focus()`, `blur()`, `press(element, key)`, `click()`, `tooltips()` and `unmount()`. `press` exists for the Radix controls that open on a key and on nothing else jsdom can produce — see the listbox surface above — and `type(element, text)`, added by the Page composer's audience pass, is how text reaches a *controlled* field: the native value setter is called (React's tracker watches that one) and a bubbling `input` is dispatched, because assigning `.value` alone is discarded by React as a change it never heard about — and `chooseFiles(input, files)`, added by the Page-editing pass, is the same idea for a file input, where `files` is read-only and jsdom has no `DataTransfer`, so the list is defined over the property and a real `change` dispatched inside `act`. `tooltips()` reads `document.body` rather than the mount container, because Radix portals the content out to the body — which is also why "is it in the page?" and "does the component render it?" are separate questions.
- **A DOM test must ask for a tick.** Radix opens a tooltip on a timer even at `delayDuration={0}`, so the test focuses the control, then calls `settle()` (a 20 ms `act`) before asserting. The tick is left to the test rather than hidden inside `focus()` on purpose: a test that forgets it should fail loudly, not hang. Pass `delayDuration={0}` to `TooltipProvider` — the default is 700 ms and waiting it out in every test is how a suite gets slow enough to be skipped. Tooltips open on hover **or** focus and only focus is reachable here, so focus is the trigger a DOM test drives; the preview browser is still the only place hover can be exercised by hand.
- **`npm install` needs `--legacy-peer-deps` in this repo, and that is pre-existing.** `package.json` declares `@cloudflare/workers-types` `^4.20250710.0` while `wrangler@4.135.0` carries a peerOptional on `^5.20260918.1`, so npm 11 aborts with `ERESOLVE` on any install, jsdom or not. Adding jsdom that way was verified additive before it was trusted: **0 lockfile lines removed, 36 packages added, `node_modules` entries 177 → 205**, checked by diffing the lockfile against a backup. Fixing the conflict properly (bumping `workers-types` to 5) would change which type errors the baseline holds, so it was left alone.
- What exists, colocated with its source and mostly pure (no database, and jsdom only where a document is the point): `src/lib/post-audiences.test.ts` (15 tests) pins the list itself — that the database enum is built from it, that every audience has a non-empty name of its own, that `isPostAudience` accepts exactly the declared audiences and rejects the near-misses (`"Public"`, `"followers "`, `null`, `7`, `["public"]`), that `toPostAudience` falls back to the first audience, and the whole `canReadPost` grid — every audience × both edges × a post that belongs to a Page and one that does not — including an audience nobody declared (author-only, matching the SQL's failure to match it). `src/lib/db/post-visibility.test.ts` (13) compiles the predicate with `new PgDialect().sqlToQuery(...)` and asserts it binds the reader to the authorship check and to both follow edges, gates `followers` on an edge from *that* reader to the *post's* subject — the author arm guarded by `page_id is null`, the Page arm reading `page_follows` — contains no `private` branch (author-only is exclusion), and renders exactly one clause (and two edge lookups) per audience the rule says admits somebody. Four more tests there render the predicate **through the query builder**, single-table and joined, because drizzle drops a table's qualifier in a single-table query's select list and `page_follows` has a `page_id` of its own — an unqualified `"page_id"` in the Page arm would compare the subquery's column to itself and admit every reader. `src/lib/db/author-timeline.test.ts` (4) is the same technique for the other half of a member's timeline: the predicate compiled with `and`, naming the author and ruling out Page posts (`page_id is null`), binding only that member's id, and binding each member's own rather than a shared value. Those two files are where the two questions the app asks of `posts` — *may this reader see it* and *is it this member's own voice* — are pinned without a database. `src/components/social/post-audience-select.test.tsx` (9) pins the menu's contents to the list and the trigger's own name — the same audiences in the same order, under the list's own names, with one distinct description each — that `audienceOptionsFor(subject)` says *whose* followers only when a Page is speaking and moves nothing else about the options, and that `AudienceIcon` draws something for every audience. `src/components/social/post-composer.test.ts` (6) covers the collapse rule as a truth table. `src/components/ui/tooltip.test.tsx` (3) asserts Radix is behind the tooltip (its `data-state` on the trigger), that the content stays out of the page until it is open, and that a missing provider throws — the three properties a pass-through stub fails. `src/components/shared/inline-notice.test.ts` renders the notice with `renderToStaticMarkup` and reaches its dismiss handler by calling the component (a pure function of its props) and walking the element tree. `src/components/ui/icon-button.test.tsx` (**13**; one of the jsdom files, `// @vitest-environment jsdom` at the top, four of its tests mounting through `src/test/render.tsx`) is where the hint/name relationship is pinned: it asserts the name is the hint when there is no `detail`, that the name is hint-plus-detail and nothing narrower when there is one (and that no `aria-label` anywhere in the markup announces the detail alone, which is the shape a WCAG 2.5.3 failure would take), that the label each control carries stays its own when two are rendered together, and that an `href` makes it an `<a href>` while its absence keeps it a `<button>`. `src/lib/search-query.test.ts` (5) pins what counts as a query and where a search goes, including the blank cases (`""`, `"   "`, `null`, `undefined` → `null` href) and the encoding of a query that is not URL-shaped. `src/components/layout/main-nav.test.tsx` (6) is the one place the decision to **wire up** the nav's search control rather than delete it is held: it renders the real `MainNav` and asserts the search control is `<a … aria-label="Search" href="/search">` and is not `<button … aria-label="Search">`. It also pins the state that is only drawn: exactly one item carries `aria-current="page"` (and it is the stubbed path's own), the others carry none, and the mobile menu button is named with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Three modules are stubbed to get there — `next/navigation` (no router in a test), `@/components/auth-provider` (the nav gates its right side on the session) and the notification bell (the notifications provider throws without a provider, and the real one would drag a Supabase browser client and a Realtime socket into a test about an `href`). The stubs are setup; the only thing asserted is what the nav itself writes. `src/components/shared/filter-chip.test.tsx` (5) pins the pressed/fill pairing both ways, including that the outlined chip does not carry the filled variant's class, and that a `surface="dark"` chip is translucent when it is off and filled when it is on — which is the cover studio's wiring, not the primitive's behaviour. `src/components/realtime/online-status.test.tsx` (5) stubs the presence hook (it reads a WebSocket that never connects here) and asserts the online, last-seen, *no-information* and visible-text cases — the `string | null` contract with the hook is the part that broke "Last seen Unknown". The picker's own name is asserted for **every** audience in the shared list, so a new audience has to answer there. `src/components/ui/media.test.tsx` (5) is a jsdom file and covers `MediaImage` — see the media section. **`src/test/a11y.test.ts` (65) is the helper's contract — names and states both — and `src/test/rendered-a11y.test.tsx` (20) is the audit over nineteen rendered surfaces**, the two halves of the check that would have caught the nameless mobile menu button; see the audit section. **`src/lib/theme.test.ts` (9)** pins the theme's *rules* — what `system` resolves to, what counts as a stored accent, and the account-versus-device precedence — and **`src/components/providers/theme-sync.test.tsx` (4)** pins the wiring that applies them; see the accent section. **`src/components/layout/theme-menu-items.test.tsx` (4)** is the nav switcher's own file — the menu's three items in the app's order, the group's name, the single `aria-checked`, the single tick, and a one-click switch that persists it; **`src/components/layout/mobile-nav-theme.test.tsx` (3)** is the same judgment for the mobile panel, which is opened through its own disclosure first; see the two nav-theme sections above. **`src/test/globals-layer.test.ts` (10)** is the stylesheet contract for `globals.css` — the layering invariant, the `@theme` token declarations, the absence of hand-written token rules, and the five `.dark`/accent blocks of the theme contract — and it is the only test here that reads a source file rather than rendering one; see the layer and theme notes above. The state conventions have their own tests besides: `src/components/ui/toggle-button.test.tsx` (8) and `src/components/ui/disclosure-button.test.tsx` (5) each pin their primitive both ways, including that a contradicting attribute pushed through a cast cannot win; `toggle-button` also pins the two surfaces, that the filled state survives on both, and — as a characterisation, not a feature — that a caller's own `bg-*` replaces the fill, which is the reason `surface` exists at all. `src/components/ui/status-indicator.test.tsx` (6) pins that the words are always present, that the mark is `aria-hidden`, that the default tone says nothing emphatic, and that a label-less status does not compile. `src/lib/r2.test.ts` (7) is the storage module's first test file and covers the two pure decisions that precede a delete — see the Page-image cleanup section for what it pins, and why `deleteStoredObjects` itself is deliberately not one of them.
- Tests should fail when the code is wrong, so check it. Deleting the follow-edge branch from `visiblePostsCondition` made 3 of its 6 tests fail. The same check on the shared rule is what the rule is for: setting `followers.requiresFollow` to `false` failed 17 tests, **11 of them the integration ones**, because the fake's answers move with the rule, where a rule copied into the fake by hand would have left all 11 green while the server changed underneath them. Appending an audience to `postAudiences` failed the build in 5 places and 3 tests. Renaming the picker's "Only me" to "Private" failed the picker test. The composer's collapse rule is a truth table over twelve situations and only one of them collapses — a bug that removed the picker's case (the one that closed the composer) fails two of its tests. Putting the tooltip back in its pass-through form failed all three of its tests, and dropping `aria-label={label}` from `IconButton` failed three of its then-four. Making the name the `detail` alone instead of `label, detail` fails the `detail` test, on its first assertion — that mutation is exactly the WCAG 2.5.3 regression the prop is shaped to prevent. Note the second `detail`-less test stays green under it, because with no `detail` the two spellings agree; the pair of tests is what covers both shapes, not either one alone. Pointing `TooltipContent` at `detail` instead of `label` fails exactly 1 of `IconButton`'s 13 — the DOM test, with `expected [ '3 unread' ] to deeply equal [ 'Notifications' ]`. That failure is the whole argument for adding the environment: before it, the tooltip's text was not assertable at all, so this exact regression would have passed every test in the suite. `MediaImage` was checked the same way, one bug reinstated at a time: copying `src` on mount again fails only *"shows a new source when the caller swaps it"*; putting the `/images/placeholder.png` default back fails only *"does not invent a fallback the app cannot serve"*; and dropping the anti-loop guard fails only *"swaps to a fallback the caller asked for, and only once"* (which is also what that guard is for). The sweep for drawn-only state was checked the same way, four mutations at once: a chip that keeps the filled variant while announcing `aria-pressed={false}` fails 2 of `filter-chip`'s 4; restoring the colour-only dot (the status text back to `{showText && …}`) fails 2 of `online-status`'s 5; putting the picker's name back to the constant "Choose post audience" fails both of the name tests; and dropping `aria-current` from the nav items fails the nav one. Collapsing `IconButton`'s link branch into the button branch fails 1 of its 13 (the link test) — and only that one, because the sibling test that a control *without* an `href` stays a button is satisfied by either spelling. Removing `href="/search"` from the nav's search control fails 2 of the 6 `main-nav` tests (the link one and the not-a-button one) — which is the exact state the app shipped in, so it is the mutation worth having run. **The accessible-name audit was checked the same way, against the code it already failed once and then fixed**: removing the listing card's `aria-label` fails exactly 1 of the 14 audit surfaces (the marketplace one), and putting the cover studio's `cover-duration` and `cover-subtitle` labels back to unattached form fails exactly 1 (the cover-studio surface, which is one test). So a control that loses its name has a test that says so by name rather than by count. **The state conventions were mutated the same way, one attribute at a time, and every one was caught by both layers**: dropping `aria-pressed` from `ToggleButton` fails 4 of its 5 tests *and* 4 of the audit's 15 surfaces (marketplace, jobs, communities, cover studio — the four chip rows); dropping `aria-expanded` from `DisclosureButton` fails 4 of its 5 and 3 of the audit's (both nav surfaces plus `the app's disclosures`); dropping the words from `StatusIndicator` fails 2 of its 6 and 4 of `online-status`'s 5; and deleting one row's `aria-label` fails exactly 1 surface, the marketplace. The pattern is worth noting: the primitive's tests fail on the mechanism and the audit fails on the pages, so neither alone would have caught every case. **The cover-studio fix was mutated too, including the failure it was shaped to avoid**: putting `bg-white/5` into `FilterChip`'s own `className` — i.e. doing it the obvious call-site way — fails 1 of its 5 tests, the one that says a chip cannot be drawn unchosen while announcing that it is chosen. Making `ToggleButton` ignore `surface` fails 2. And setting `PANEL` back to `border-white/10`, which is the bug as it actually shipped, fails **nothing**: no test can see a background colour, because jsdom computes no CSS. That one is guarded by a measurement and a screenshot, and the runbook is where that difference is written down. **The layering invariant was mutated three ways, and each hit its own assertion:** pulling `.bg-accent` back out of a layer failed 2 (the invariant, naming the rule in its message, and the then-current token-in-a-layer check); unwrapping `* { border-color }` from `@layer base` failed 2, including `leaves the border default layered` — which is the bug from the pass before that, so the guard covered it too; and deleting `.bg-popover` outright failed 1, the positive check. **The `@theme` rewrite was mutated the same way, at three levels of scope:** deleting the single line `--color-ring: hsl(var(--ring))` from the `@theme inline` block fails exactly 1 — *"declares every semantic token in @theme…"*, with `expected [ 'ring' ] to deeply equal []`; adding a hand-written `.text-muted-foreground { color: … }` back inside a `@layer utilities` block fails exactly 1 — *"leaves those token classes to Tailwind instead of hand-writing them"*, naming `text-muted-foreground` — and, notably, *not* the unlayered-colour invariant, because it is inside a layer; and restoring the **entire pre-change stylesheet** fails 3 of the 5 (both token assertions plus the sanity check, since the old file has one `@theme` block of 20 declarations rather than two). So the deletion of the twenty rules is covered in both directions: a token that stops being declared, and a rule that comes back. All were run against the final file through its `?raw` import, and `globals.css` was `md5sum`-verified back to its pre-mutation value after each (the current file is `b616da01d0aca5a48372269cfaa52161`), because a mutation harness that leaves the subject changed is worse than none. Do this once per new suite — a green suite that asserts nothing is worse than none.
- `src/lib/feed-audience.test.ts` pins the feed's audience decisions (`followLossEffect`, `mergeRevealedPosts`, `visibilityChangeNeedsRecheck`, `revealNoticeMessage`, `newestFirst`) as units — these are the functions `src/app/(main)/feed/page.tsx` calls, lifted out of the component in `src/lib/feed-audience.ts` so they can be read and tested on their own.
- `src/lib/feed-audience.integration.test.ts` drives the flows a reader actually causes — a follow reveals posts, an unfollow drops them, an edit that narrows an audience removes the card, and a Page's followers-only post belonging to the Page's followers rather than its admin's — as whole sequences through those same real functions, asserting on what is left on screen (`25` tests). It is there because the rules interact: a revealed post can be narrowed later, an unfollow can arrive for an author whose cards came from an earlier reveal, and a recheck must not disturb what it was not asked about.
- **What stands in for the world there is a fake `GET /api/posts`**, since this repo has no test database, no Testing Library and no DOM unless a file asks for one. The fake answers the two shapes the feed uses — `?authorId=` and `?ids=` — and applies the audience rule by *calling* it — `canReadPost` from `src/lib/post-audiences.ts`, the in-process half of the rule `visiblePostsCondition` is rendered from — rather than by restating it. What is still pinned separately, in `post-visibility.test.ts`, is the SQL *shape* the rule is rendered into, since no test here can evaluate SQL. The harness also mirrors the page's handlers (`revealAuthorPosts`, `revalidateVisiblePosts`, `applyFollowChange`, the `posts` UPDATE handler), including their order, because the order is part of the behaviour. Its world holds **two** follow graphs, member and Page, because the rule now asks two questions; the Page one is exercised only by the Page tests, since a Page follow never reaches the feed.
- **A trap that made 5 of the new tests fail first:** the fake world and the feed held the *same* post objects, so mutating the server's row also mutated the mounted card — silently closing the very `visibility` change the test meant to observe, and making `visibilityChangeNeedsRecheck` see no change at all. The API and `load()` now return copies (`clonePost`), because the real client only ever gets JSON. Any future fake has to do the same.
- Verified live after the refactor, against the running app and the seeded database (all rows restored: 67 live / 69, 0 non-public, 0 edited, 32 follows, viewer follows nobody, 0 probes): narrowing a mounted other-author post to `followers` removed its card and the `GET /api/posts?ids=` recheck was observed in the network log; following that author brought the card back; unfollowing dropped it again.

## Pages (public accounts)

- **A Page is a public account that is not a person** — a brand, a business or a community with its own name, its own posts and its own followers. The model was already half in the schema and entirely unusable: `pages`, `page_roles` and `posts.page_id` existed, and one route reached them, but there was no page, no creation UI and nothing that read a role. It was also **wrong in one load-bearing way**: `GET /api/pages` counted a Page's followers with `follows.following_id = page.id`, but that column is a foreign key to `users.id`, so the number could only ever be zero. A Page has no id `follows` could hold, which is why the fix is a table and not a query.
- **`page_follows` (migration `0010_pages_public`)** is that table: `(page_id, user_id)` unique, both columns cascading, and an index on `user_id` for the other direction. Written the way 0009 records — every statement `IF NOT EXISTS`, because `drizzle-kit migrate` cannot be used here (the tracking table is empty while the schema is already pushed) and migrations are applied directly. The foreign keys sit **inline in the `CREATE TABLE`** rather than as `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT`: Postgres has no `ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS`, but a skipped `CREATE TABLE` takes its inline constraints with it, so the file stays idempotent. Apply it with `node --env-file-if-exists=.env.local .freebuff/apply-migration.mjs drizzle/0010_pages_public.sql` (and `Remove-Item Env:DATABASE_URL` first, as with every other DB command here).
- **The API**: `GET /api/pages?username=` returns the Page with `stats {followers, posts}`, the viewer's `isFollowing` and the viewer's `role`; `GET /api/pages` is the directory, counting followers in a subquery (an inner join would drop a Page nobody follows); `POST` creates the Page **and the first `page_roles` row**, which is the half the old route left out — without it, not even the creator could post as their own Page; `PUT`/`DELETE` require the `admin` role; `POST /api/pages/follow` mirrors the member route's contract (explicit `following`, `onConflictDoNothing`, and the new total returned) against the new table. `DELETE` also removes the Page's posts explicitly, because `posts.page_id` deliberately has no foreign key (neither does `posts.group_id`), so nothing would cascade them.
- **Posting as a Page keeps a real author.** `POST /api/posts` accepts `pageId`, checks the caller is an admin of that Page, and writes `author_id` as the person and `page_id` as the Page. Ownership, edits and deletes keep comparing against `author_id` and so keep working; the Page is the identity shown. `GET /api/posts` gained a validated `?pageId=` filter and returns the Page beside the author, so a caller can tell the two apart. The Page view passes **the Page** to `PostCard`, not the payload's `author` — rendering the author would credit every Page post to whoever happened to be signed in, which is what `src/components/pages/page-view.test.tsx` pins by asserting the admin's name appears nowhere.
- **The UI**: `/pages` (directory + Create), `/pages/new` (the form, validating the username against the same rule the API enforces), and `/pages/[username]` — the Page's own page, with the Follow control for everyone and the "Post as <Page>" composer only for an admin, whose `role` comes from the server rather than from comparing ids, because a Page can have more than one admin. `Pages` joined the nav and `Create a Page` the account menu. **"Public" means *not a person*, not *not signed in***: every route still requires a session, as the whole app does.
- **A small extraction came with it**: `formatPostTime` was duplicated verbatim in the feed and the profile page, so it moved to `src/lib/post-time.ts` and all three import it rather than the Page view becoming a third copy.
- **Tests**: `src/components/pages/page-view.test.tsx` (7 by the end of the editing pass, jsdom, the eighth jsdom file) pins the things that are the view's own — a post carries the *Page's* identity and the admin's name is absent; the composer is offered to an admin and not to a visitor; and a follow sends `{pageId, following: true}` rather than a toggle and adopts the server's new follower total. `src/test/rendered-a11y.test.tsx` gained a surface, `a Page, with an admin's composer` (**19 tests over eighteen surfaces**, then **20 over nineteen** once the Page composer's audience menu was added — see the section below), which is what judges the new header, the follow control and the composer for names and states. The audit needed one addition to work at all: `useParams` in its `next/navigation` mock, since the view reads its route segment. **Confirmed the composer gate bites**: replacing `role === "admin"` with `Boolean(role)` fails exactly 1 — the composer test, on its `"member"` iteration — which is the whole reason that iteration exists; a role-bearing non-admin must not be able to speak for the Page. Reverted, `md5sum` verified.
- **The feed had to be taught whose post it is.** `GET /api/posts` now returns `page` beside `author`, and the feed's card prefers it, because rendering `author` would credit every Page post to the admin who pressed publish. Measured on `/feed` after publishing as the Page: the card reads `Northwind Studio@northwind_studio`, and the admin's name is nowhere in it. The optimistic card (created before the server answers) has no `page`, so it still falls back to `author` — correct, because a post being typed is the person's until it is published as the Page.
- **The two voices are separated on the timeline, and the rule lives in one place.** A Page's posts also appear on the **admin's personal profile** under the old filter, because the profile asks for `?authorId=<member>` and a Page post's `author_id` is that member. `?authorId=` now means *what this member said*, not *rows attributable to this member*: `src/lib/db/author-timeline.ts` exports `authoredByMember(authorId)` — `author_id = <member> AND page_id IS NULL` — returned as a condition list the route spreads into its own stack, so the two halves cannot be split up by a later edit. Nothing is lost: a Page's posts are still read back through `?pageId=` on the Page and still reach the feed, where the card is labelled with the Page; the profile's Photos/Videos tabs (`?authorId=&limit=100`) drop Page media with it, which is the same question asked about attachments. The feed's post-follow reveal (`revealAuthorPosts`, which also calls `?authorId=`) inherits the exclusion, and that is the better reading rather than a casualty: its notice names the *member* — "N new posts from Theo Wu" — which would have announced a Page's post under the wrong name, and those posts arrive on the next ordinary fetch anyway, since the reveal is only ever the head start.
- **Verified live, against the running app and the demo Page.** `GET /api/posts?pageId=<northwind_studio id>` still returns its post (page `northwind_studio`, author `theowumicrosoft`), while `GET /api/posts?authorId=<that admin>` returns **three posts, every one with `page: null`** and the Page's post absent from the list. On `/profile` the Posts tile reads **3** (it read 4 before), the three cards are the member's own, and the string `Northwind Studio` does not appear anywhere on the page; in particular the Page post's text (`We just opened our Page.`) is gone. Mutation: removing `isNull(posts.pageId)` from `authoredByMember` fails **exactly 1** of its 4 tests — *"rules out the Pages the member runs"*, `expected '"posts"."author_id" = $1' to match /"page_id" is null/i` — with the other three green, which is the shape that says the guard is specific. Reverted, `md5sum` verified.
- **Verified live, end to end, in the running app** (the migration applied first, 3 statements): `/pages` renders the empty directory; `Create a Page` → `/pages/northwind_studio`, **and the creator is an admin** — `GET /api/pages?username=northwind_studio` answered `role: "admin"`, which is the row the old route never read; the composer published a post and the Page's feed showed it credited to the Page; the follow flipped to `Unfollow` with `aria-pressed="true"` and the header to the server's `1 follower`; and the API then reported `stats {followers: 1, posts: 1}`, `isFollowing: true`. **Left behind on purpose at the time, since removed entirely:** the Page `northwind_studio` with one post and the viewer's follow row was the artifact to look at when reviewing this feature, and `DELETE /api/pages?id=<pageId>` removes the posts and the follow with it. It was deleted, along with its storage, in the Page-deletion pass — see that section.
- **Baselines after this pass:** `npm test -- --run` = **259 passed / 26 files**, `npx tsc --noEmit` = **51 errors** (unchanged), `npm run build` complete. The four new tests are `src/lib/db/author-timeline.test.ts`, which is a node file, so the jsdom count stays at eight.

## The subject of a `followers` post (a Page's posts belong to the Page)

- **Why this was a real defect and not a nicety.** `followers` was gated on `follows.following_id = posts.author_id`, and a Page's post records `author_id` as the admin who pressed publish. So a Page's followers-only post was readable by the *admin's* followers and invisible to the Page's own — the audience named on the post, and the audience the Page spent effort collecting, were different people. The fix is in the rule and its two renderings; see the audiences section for the clause itself, the `page_id is null` guard that makes the author arm inapplicable rather than merely weaker, and the live check against the development database.
- **The client had to be told, because it keeps its own copy of the rule.** `followLossEffect` dropped *any* `followers` card by the member when the viewer unfollowed them — which would have removed a Page's post that the viewer can still read, the moment they stopped following its admin. It now drops only the member's own voice and sends a Page's card to `GET /api/posts?ids=`, which is the same "never guess, ask the server" posture the rest of the feed uses for an audience it cannot settle. `AudiencePost` gained `page`, and the doc comment says why the member edge says nothing about a Page post.
- **Following a Page now re-reads the Page's posts, which is the mirror of the feed's reveal.** The Page view fetched its posts once, so the edge that had just moved changed what was readable with nothing on screen to show it — in *both* directions, since an unfollow narrows it back. The follow control's `onChange` calls `loadPosts` again rather than patching the list: the server decides what the new edge admits. `page-view.test.tsx` pins it by making the stubbed endpoint return the followers-only post only after the click, so the assertion is about what appears rather than about a request count.
- **Mutations, each reverted with `md5sum` verified.** Dropping the `page_id is null` guard from the author arm fails **exactly 3** — all in `post-visibility.test.ts`: the guard's own test, the correlated-reference count, and the query-builder test that asserts the qualified `"posts"."page_id" is null`. It fails *nothing* in `post-audiences` or the integration suite, which is the point of the two renderings being tested separately. Making `canReadPost` always use the author edge fails **exactly 6** — 4 integration (a Page's post readable by the admin's follower, unreadable by the Page's, staying, leaving) and 2 unit — and **nothing** in `post-visibility.test.ts`, the mirror image of the first mutation. Making `followLossEffect` drop Page cards again fails **exactly 3** (2 unit, 1 integration flow). Removing the Page view's re-read fails **exactly 1**, the new view test.
- **Verified live, through the running app.** Publishing a `followers` post as the demo Page (via `POST /api/posts` with `pageId`) made it appear in `?pageId=` with `visibility: "followers"`, appear on `/pages/northwind_studio` credited to the Page with the **Followers** pill beside the time, and stay *absent* from the admin's `?authorId=` timeline — both rules holding at once, which is the pair that used to be crossed. The post was deleted afterwards, so the demo Page is back to its one public post.
- **The Page composer chooses its audience, so the rule is reachable from the UI.** It had one hard-coded `visibility: "public"`; it now renders the same `<PostAudienceSelect>` the feed and the profile use, sends what it is set to, and starts at `public` because a Page is a public account. All three audiences are offered, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight: the server rule enforces all three for a Page's post, and the list that the picker is built from is the same list the rule is — offering a subset would be a second decision to keep in step.
- **The picker had to learn who is speaking, or its copy would lie.** `audienceDescription` was a constant written for the member typing ("People who follow you"), and the people who can read a Page's followers-only post are the *Page's* followers — the same crossing the rule was fixed for, one layer up in the UI. It is now `audienceOptionsFor(subject)`: `null` for the member, a Page's name when a Page is speaking, and only the `followers` sentence differs, because it is the only one whose meaning depends on it. `public` and `private` say the same thing either way, and `private` is worth stating: "Visible just to you" is still true of an admin's `private` post on a Page. The names, the order and the two unchanged descriptions are pinned as unchanged, so a subject can only move the one sentence that depends on it.
- **A jsdom test drives that picker for the first time, and the browser agreed with it.** `page-view.test.tsx` types into the Page composer, opens the menu with a real `keydown` on its trigger, walks to `Followers`, and asserts the published body is `{content, pageId, visibility: "followers"}`. That needed one new helper — `mount().type()`, which sets a controlled input through the native value setter and dispatches `input`, the shape React's value tracker watches — because the suite had no way to put text in a field. Radix's `DropdownMenu` is drivable this way in jsdom (Enter on the trigger, `ArrowDown`, `Enter`), which is the first interactive coverage the shared picker has had; until now it was pinned only as markup. **Confirmed live in the same order**: on `/pages/northwind_studio` the trigger focused and opened on `Enter`, the menu rendered `Public — Anyone on and off LinkMe+`, `Followers — People who follow Northwind Studio`, `Only me — Visible just to you` under a group named `Post audience`, two `ArrowDown`s and `Enter` set the trigger to `Post audience: Followers`, and publishing stored `visibility: "followers"` on `northwind_studio`'s post, which then appeared on the Page with the Followers pill. The trigger was clicked first and nothing opened — Radix still will not open from a synthesised pointer here, exactly as the runbook says of the settings select, and the key path is what works. (The post was deleted afterwards.)
- **The audience menu is now an audited surface.** Its options exist only while it is open, so nothing else could judge them: `rendered-a11y.test.tsx` gained `the Page composer's audience menu, opened`, which opens it with a key and **states that a `menuitemradio` is in the document** before the audit runs, then judges the named group and each option's `aria-checked`. Mutating the group's `aria-label` away fails **exactly that one surface** with `[unnamed-group] a group of options has no name, so nothing says what is being chosen between`, echoing the real `<div role="group">` — the same failure mode the theme switcher's group was caught by, now covered where the app's most-used menu lives. Reverted, `md5sum` verified.
- **The other three mutations, each reverted with `md5sum` verified.** Hard-coding the Page composer's `visibility: "public"` fails **exactly 1** — the publishing test, on the body — and leaves the picker's own file green, because a component test cannot see what a page sends. Dropping `asPage` from the Page composer fails **exactly 1** as well, the same test, now on the copy — and again nothing in `post-audience-select.test.tsx`, where the option function is exercised directly: mechanism and wiring fail separately, which is what makes both worth having. Making `audienceOptionsFor` ignore its subject fails **exactly 2** (the copy test and the page-view one), and *not* the "changes nothing else" test, which is why that one is written as a comparison with the member's options rather than as more prose.
- **Baselines after the picker, which landed in the same working session:** the rule added sixteen tests and the picker four more (2 in `post-audience-select.test.tsx`, 1 in `page-view.test.tsx`, 1 audit surface), so **279 passed / 26 files** on the code this section describes — 275 + 19, with nothing removed and no new files. `npx tsc --noEmit` = **51 errors** (unchanged) and `npm run build` complete. The seven files this passes touched run green together: **107 tests** in `page-view.test.tsx`, `post-audience-select.test.tsx`, `rendered-a11y.test.tsx`, `post-visibility.test.ts`, `post-audiences.test.ts`, `feed-audience.test.ts` and `feed-audience.integration.test.ts`.
- **The checkout is shared, and that has to be read as data rather than noise.** While this section was being written the tree moved under it twice: one suite invocation reported `2 failed | 277 passed` and `tsc` reported **71** errors naming files this session never touched (`src/app/api/auth/phone/send-otp/route.ts`, `src/hooks/use-websocket.ts`), and minutes later the run after it reported **291 passed / 28 files** — two test files and twelve tests that are not this pass's — with `tsc` back at 51 and the build still complete. So: re-run before believing a failure, check the file list in an error before attributing it, and treat the *number* as a property of the checkout at that moment rather than of the last edit. The 279 above is this work's own contribution, not a claim about the tree today.

## Editing a Page from the Page itself

- **What was missing was the UI, not the API.** `PUT /api/pages` already accepted `name`, `description`, `categoryId`, `avatarUrl` and `coverUrl` and already required the `admin` role — and nothing called it. The Page now carries an **Edit Page** control for admins (the same `role === "admin"` gate the composer reads, from the server rather than from comparing ids) which opens `src/components/pages/page-edit-dialog.tsx`: name, description, Page photo and cover. The view merges what the dialog reports (`onSaved`) into its own `page` state, so the header, the cover and the composer's labels update without a refetch. The username is deliberately *not* a field: it is the Page's address (`/pages/<username>`), so changing it is a redirect question, and every post and follow row points at the Page by id.
- **One upload route for both images** (`POST /api/pages/image`, multipart `file` + `pageId` + `kind`), rather than the two the member profile has: nothing differs between a Page photo and a cover except a column and a storage folder, and the part that must not exist twice is the authorization. `kind` is validated against one `TARGETS` map, the role is checked **before** the object is written so a refused upload leaves nothing in the bucket, and the key is built from the **Page's** id — the photo belongs to the Page and outlives its admins, and a Page with several admins would otherwise scatter one photo across their folders. Verified live: the stored keys are `avatars/<pageId>/<ts>-<rand>.png` and `covers/<pageId>/<ts>-<rand>.png`.
- **The dialog writes in two shapes on purpose.** Name and description are one `PUT` with a Save button; a photo or cover is stored the moment it is chosen, like a member's own photo, and reported to the Page immediately — there is nothing left for Save to do about an image, and pretending otherwise would let somebody close the dialog believing their choice had been discarded. The dialog says which succeeded ("Page photo updated.") and which failed, in its own `role="status"`/`role="alert"` lines.
- **A live check found a real bug the tests had not: the form re-seeded itself on every render.** The upload reports back to the Page, which flows in again as a changed prop — and a seeding effect with those props in its deps therefore wiped the notice *and* any half-typed name. It now seeds on the **open transition** (`open && !wasOpen.current`), with the reason written where the effect is. Both halves matter: seeding on mount would show a stale Page to a reopened dialog, and seeding on every render silently discards work. **The bug is now pinned by a test** — `keeps unsaved text when a photo is uploaded next to it` types a name, chooses a file, and asserts the name is still there and the upload was reported — and reverting the effect to the buggy form fails **exactly 1**, `expected 'Northwind Studio' to be 'Northwind Works'`. Reverted, `md5sum` verified.
- **`PUT /api/pages` was tightened where the form now exercises it.** It applied the *create* path's limits to neither `description` (now capped at 500, trimmed, `null`-able) nor `categoryId` (now a validated uuid, so a bad one is a 400 rather than a 500 out of the column cast), and it cast anything at all into `avatarUrl`/`coverUrl` (now a string, `null`, or absent — one helper, `readText`, reads all four fields, and a number is a 400; that route also removes the image an update displaces, see the replacement section above). Verified live, each refused by name and with the Page left intact: unknown `kind` → `400 An image kind of "avatar" or "cover" is required`; non-uuid `pageId` → `400 Invalid page id`; no file → `400 An image file is required`; `PUT` with an unknown Page id → `403 Only a Page admin can edit it` (the role check runs first, so the answer does not reveal whether the Page exists); a 501-character description → `400`; `avatarUrl: 42` → `400 An image url must be a string or null`; a 101-character name → `400`.
- **Two new helpers came out of this pass, both in `src/test/render.tsx`.** `chooseFiles(input, files)` selects files and fires the real `change` — `files` is read-only and jsdom has no `DataTransfer`, so the list is defined over the property and the event is dispatched inside `act`. And the stub in `page-view.test.tsx` now keeps a multipart body **whole** instead of `JSON.parse(String(body))`: the first version threw `Unexpected token 'o', "[object FormData]" is not valid JSON` on the upload, inside the mock, which read exactly like the component never calling `fetch` at all. A mock that cannot express a request is a mock that reports a false negative.
- **A flake removed rather than tolerated.** The audience-picker test chose `Followers` by walking the menu with arrow keys, and that raced Radix's focus scheduling — it failed once in roughly ten runs with `no control named "Post audience: Followers" was rendered`. It now clicks the option itself (`[role="menuitemradio"]` containing "Followers"), keeps the copy assertion, and passed three consecutive runs. Radix's keyboard behaviour is its own business and is still what the audit surface and the live check use.
- **The open dialog is an audited surface**: `a Page, with the edit dialog opened` opens it and **states that a `[role="dialog"]` is in the document** before the audit runs. It is the first surface here where Radix hides the page behind the dialog, so the dialog's own controls are the whole subject. Mutating the two image buttons to drop their words fails **exactly that one surface**, with `2 control(s) with no accessible name` — and leaves `a Page, with an admin's composer` green, which is the proof the surface is what reaches into the portal. Reverted, `md5sum` verified.
- **Also mutated, each reverted with `md5sum` verified**: widening the Edit control's gate from `isAdmin` to `Boolean(role)` fails **exactly 1** — the non-admin half of the gate test, which is the half that matters (a Page can have members who are not admins); and dropping `id` from the dialog's `PUT` body fails **exactly 1**, the rename test, on the body it sent.
- **What the tests cannot see, and what was therefore verified live instead.** There are no route tests here, so the upload route's own behaviour — the role check, the key, the stored URL — is verified only by the live runs above, and the two image rows are driven in jsdom through the dialog's file input with a `File` built in the test. **Verified live end to end, in the running app, with R2 configured**: with the dialog open, a canvas-generated PNG chosen for the Page photo stored `avatars/b63fc2b0-…/1790350237900-3p84r9.png` and rendered in the header; a second for the cover stored `covers/b63fc2b0-…/1790350658160-vuh7xb.png`, which the browser then loaded and decoded (`naturalWidth 480`) — the object really is in the bucket and publicly readable, not merely recorded. Typing a new name, uploading the cover, and saving left the header reading `Northwind Studio Renamed` with the dialog closed; the name and description were then set back to `Northwind Studio` / "A studio that makes things." so the demo Page's identity is unchanged. **Left in place at the time:** the Page photo and cover uploaded during that check, so the artifact showed the feature working. Both objects were later deleted with the Page — see the Page-deletion section.
- **Baselines after this pass:** `npm test -- --run` = **303 passed / 29 files** in the checkout as it stands, of which this pass added 2 tests (one in `page-view.test.tsx`, one audit surface) — the rest of the movement is other work landing in the same tree. `npx tsc --noEmit` = **51 errors** (unchanged), `npm run build` complete. The two files this pass touched that are part of that suite run green together: `page-view.test.tsx` (7) and `rendered-a11y.test.tsx` (21).

## Replacing a Page's photo or cover deletes the object it displaced

- **The upload route overwrote the column and left the old object in the bucket.** `POST /api/pages/image` stored `avatars/<pageId>/<ts>-<rand>.png`, pointed `pages.avatar_url` (or `cover_url`) at it and returned — while the object the previous URL named stayed in storage and kept answering publicly, so every change of a Page photo or cover cost one more file forever. It now reads that column **before** the update and hands the previous URL to `deleteStoredObjects`, the same cleanup `DELETE /api/posts` already applies to a post's media.
- **The order is forced, and so is the scope of the read.** `.returning()` asks Postgres for the row as it now is, so the displaced URL stops being recorded anywhere the moment the update lands — it has to be read first, or it can never be found again. Only the column for this `kind` is read, so replacing a photo cannot reach the cover. The read is a plain `db.select`, not wrapped in `withDbRetry`, matching the role check above it and the posts route's own read.
- **The decision is its own pure function, and it is tested: `replacedObjectUrl(previous, next)` in `src/lib/r2.ts`.** It reports the URL a write displaced, and `null` when there was nothing there or when the URL is the one being written again. That equality guard is not ceremony: keys are timestamp-plus-random, so an upload that somehow resolved to the key already stored would report the URL it had just overwritten, and deleting it would destroy the file the row is now showing. `next` is typed `string | null` rather than `string | undefined` on purpose — a caller with something to write always has one, either a URL or the `null` that clears the column — so "this write does not touch the field" is refused by the compiler rather than left to a caller to remember.
- **Nothing is deleted from a guessed key.** `deleteStoredObjects` maps each URL through `keyFromPublicUrl`, which returns `null` unless the URL actually begins with `R2_PUBLIC_URL` *and its slash* — `https://…r2.dev.evil.example.com/x.png` is foreign, not ours — and it swallows per-object failures, so a storage hiccup cannot turn an upload the row already records into an error the admin sees. A Page whose column holds an external image URL (the seeded ones do) is left alone rather than mis-deleted.
- **New tests: `src/lib/r2.test.ts` (7).** The module had none, and the two functions that decide whether a delete happens are pure — `deleteStoredObjects` itself cannot be exercised without a bucket or a mocked SDK, but the question it asks first can, which is why the file stops there. It pins `keyFromPublicUrl` (recovers a key; strips a query or fragment a URL may have picked up; refuses a foreign host, a host whose name merely *begins* with ours, the bare origin, the bare prefix, and the empty/`null`/`undefined` cases) and `replacedObjectUrl` (reports a displaced URL — including a `null` that clears the column; reports nothing for an empty column; reports nothing when the URL is unchanged, with a near-miss beside it so that guard cannot pass by always returning nothing; and reports nothing for a field the write never mentioned — the `undefined` an absent key in a partial update carries).
- **Mutations, each reverted with `md5sum` verified** (`src/lib/r2.ts` `98722faea11b232cc3bb508714a678b2`, `src/app/api/pages/route.ts` `f85d46ace8f687d28983f20557d140db`): dropping the equality guard (`if (!previous || next === undefined || previous === next)` → `if (!previous)`) fails **exactly 1** — *"reports nothing when the same URL is written again"*, `expected 'https://test.r2.dev/avatars/page-1/same.png' to be null`. Weakening the prefix rail to `url.startsWith(PUBLIC_URL)` while leaving key extraction correct fails **exactly 1** — *"refuses a URL that is not ours"*, `expected '.evil.example.com/photo.jpg' to be null` — so the host check is covered on its own rather than only through the extraction. (A first attempt replaced the whole prefix with the bare origin and failed 3, because the extracted key then kept its leading slash; it was narrowed to the mutation above so the failure names the rail rather than the extraction.) And dropping the `next === undefined` arm — the guard that stops a rename from deleting the Page's photo — fails **exactly 1**, *"reports nothing for a field the write never mentioned"*, `expected 'https://test.r2.dev/avatars/page-1/kept.png' to be null`.
- **What no test here can reach is the route's own wiring, so that was verified live, on the running app, against the real bucket.** The demo Page's photo and cover were each replaced *through the route itself*, in the page's own signed-in session (`fetch("/api/pages/image", {method:"POST", body})` with a canvas-generated PNG in a `FormData` — exactly the shape the edit dialog sends), and the objects were then asked for directly with `curl`:

  | object | before the replacement | after |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | the replaced photo (`avatars/…/1790350237900-3p84r9.png`) | `200`, 1085 B | **`404`** |
  | the photo that replaced it (`avatars/…/1790352368571-93i9us.png`) | — | `200`, 2562 B |
  | the cover, a *different* `kind` | `200` | `200` unchanged |
  | the replaced cover (`covers/…/1790350658160-vuh7xb.png`) | `200`, 18621 B | **`404`** |
  | the cover that replaced it (`covers/…/1790352388106-dx49ft.png`) | — | `200` |
  | the photo, after the cover was replaced | `200` | `200` unchanged |

  Each upload answered `200` and the Page's JSON then named the new URL, which the header rendered decoded (`480×192` cover, `200×200` photo — the object really is in the bucket and publicly readable, not merely recorded). The two "unchanged" rows matter as much as the 404s: one `kind` cannot delete the other's object. **Left in place at the time**, as the artifact: the Page then carried `avatars/b63fc2b0-…/1790352368571-93i9us.png` and `covers/b63fc2b0-…/1790352388106-dx49ft.png`, replacing the pair the editing pass uploaded. Both of those objects, and the Page they belonged to, have since been deleted — see the Page-deletion section below.
- **`PUT /api/pages` is wired through the same rule, so an image URL set or cleared by a request is cleaned up too.** It already accepted `avatarUrl`/`coverUrl` and could displace an object with no caller exercising it — the edit dialog sends only `{id, name, description}` — so the day anything wrote those fields it would have leaked, silently, on that path alone. It now reads both columns before the update (the same order, and for the same reason, as the upload route) and offers both to `replacedObjectUrl`; the helper is what knows that an absent field (`undefined`) displaces nothing, that a `null` clearing a photo does, and that re-writing an identical URL does not. Nothing about the response changed.
- **Verified live on a throwaway Page, and the *rename* case is the one that was worth proving.** A probe Page was created, given a photo and a cover by upload, then driven through three `PUT`s: setting `avatarUrl` to another stored URL, renaming the Page with **no image fields at all**, and clearing the cover with `coverUrl: null`. Afterwards the displaced photo and the cleared cover were both `404` — and the *current* photo, the one the rename had to leave alone, was still `200`. That last row is the assertion a naive `deleteStoredObjects([configured.avatarUrl, configured.coverUrl])` would fail: a rename would then delete the Page's photo every time. All three `PUT`s answered `200`, the response carried the new `avatarUrl` and a `null` cover, and deleting the Page at the end took that last object with it (`404`) and left `{pages: 0, page_roles: 0, page_follows: 0, page_posts: 0, notifications: 0}`.
- **A race that no amount of ordering fixes, recorded so it is not later mistaken for correctness.** Two uploads of the same `kind` in flight at once can both read the same previous URL: the second deletes it, the first's delete of it is a harmless no-op, and whichever object lost the race is left unreferenced. A displaced-object delete is a read-then-write and this app holds no per-Page lock; the posts route's cleanup has the same shape.

## Deleting a Page takes everything it owned with it

- **`DELETE /api/pages` left three kinds of object behind.** It removed the Page's posts explicitly (`posts.page_id` has no foreign key, so nothing cascades them) and the Page itself, which cascades `page_roles` and `page_follows` — but the Page's photo and cover live on the row that was going, and the posts it hard-deleted took their `post_media` rows with them without anything ever reaching R2. A deleted Page therefore left a photo, a cover and one object per deleted post in the bucket, all still answering at their public URLs.
- **The URLs are read before anything is deleted, and that order is the whole implementation.** After the deletes no record is left that could map a URL back to a key, so the route reads `pages.avatar_url`/`cover_url` and the Page's `post_media` URLs (`innerJoin(posts, eq(postMedia.postId, posts.id))`, filtered on `posts.page_id`) first, then deletes the rows, then hands what it read to `deleteStoredObjects`. That function refuses anything that is not ours and swallows per-object failures, so a storage hiccup cannot fail a deletion the rows already committed.
- **Verified live, end to end, on the demo Page — which is now gone.** A Page post *with a real uploaded image* was created first (through `POST /api/posts/media` and then `POST /api/posts` with `pageId`, in the page's own signed-in session), so the media half of the cleanup was exercised rather than assumed. Before the delete all three objects answered `200`; `DELETE /api/pages?id=<pageId>` answered `200 {success: true}`; afterwards every one of them was `404`:

  | object | before the delete | after |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | the Page photo (`avatars/b63fc2b0-…/1790352368571-93i9us.png`) | `200` | **`404`** |
  | the Page cover (`covers/b63fc2b0-…/1790352388106-dx49ft.png`) | `200` | **`404`** |
  | the probe post's image (`posts/42c09874-…/1790352714378-6ngwi3.png`) | `200` | **`404`** |

- **The database is empty of it too, checked rather than inferred from the cascade.** A read-only query over `pages`, `page_roles`, `page_follows`, `posts` where `page_id is not null`, and the `post_media` rows of those posts returned `{"pages":0,"page_roles":0,"page_follows":0,"page_posts":0,"page_post_media":0}`.
- **The app handles its absence the way it should.** `GET /api/pages?username=northwind_studio` is `404`, `GET /api/posts?pageId=` returns nothing, the directory reads "No Pages yet — Create the first one and it will show up here.", and `/pages/northwind_studio` renders "Page not found — No Page is using that address. It may have been renamed or removed." with a Browse Pages link. **The demo Page that several earlier Pages sections name as the artifact to look at is therefore gone, deliberately, at the owner's request** — so any recipe in this runbook that says "look at `/pages/northwind_studio`" now needs a Page created first (`Create a Page`) rather than a lookup. That is also why the two older "left behind/left in place on purpose" sentences above now read as history.
- **This pass added no test, because there was no way to reach a route from a test — and the next pass built one.** The live run above is still the evidence that the real bucket was cleaned, but the *wiring* it proves by hand is now pinned in a route-level harness: see **Testing an API route without a browser** below. The part of the deletion that is pure ("is this URL ours", "was anything displaced") is covered by `src/lib/r2.test.ts`; what `src/app/api/pages/route.test.ts` adds is that the route reads the URLs *before* it deletes the rows and hands all of them — the photo, the cover and every post's media — to `deleteStoredObjects`, and that a non-admin's delete reaches none of it.- **Baselines after this work**, which is three parts of one thing — the replacement cleanup, the Page deletion, and the `PUT` wiring. Its own contribution is **7 tests in one new file** (`src/lib/r2.test.ts`, all green) plus the two route changes. The suite total could not be read cleanly at the end, because another session was refactoring the audience list while it was being measured: consecutive runs reported **2 failed | 307 passed** and then **7 failed | 302 passed (309)**, every failure in `post-audience-select.test.tsx` or `post-visibility.test.ts` — neither of which imports `lib/r2` or `api/pages` at all — while this work's own slice (`src/lib/r2.test.ts` + `src/components/pages/page-view.test.tsx`) stayed green at **14/14**. The earlier clean reading was **309 / 30**, taken before this work's seventh test, so the arithmetic no longer closes on its own: the refactor has moved the count inside its own files too, which is why the header above still says 309. `npx tsc --noEmit` read **51** and, minutes later, **52** — the extra one a bare `process` another session had just written into `src/test/rendered-a11y.test.tsx`, whose error line moved from **226** to **240** between two runs, which is how a file being edited underfoot announces itself. **Neither of this work's two files has ever contributed a type error.** `npm run build` completed on every run, including the ones with the dirty suite. Read every number here as a property of the checkout at that moment, not of the last edit.

## Testing an API route without a browser

- **The route handlers are now reachable from a test, so the wiring the live bucket probes used to prove by hand is pinned instead.** The gap was narrow and specific: `src/lib/r2.test.ts` covers the pure decisions that precede a delete (`keyFromPublicUrl`, `replacedObjectUrl`), but nothing could reach `POST /api/pages/image`, `PUT /api/pages` or `DELETE /api/pages` at all, so *which URL the route offers up* — and whether it reads it before the write, and whether the role check runs before the object is stored — was only ever checked against the real bucket. Nine files close it for the Page, post and profile routes: `src/app/api/pages/image/route.test.ts` (5 tests), `src/app/api/pages/route.test.ts` (6), `src/app/api/posts/route.test.ts` (13), `src/app/api/posts/comments/route.test.ts` (6), `src/app/api/posts/reactions/route.test.ts` (6), `src/app/api/profile/avatar/route.test.ts` (6), `src/app/api/profile/cover/route.test.ts` (5), `src/app/api/profile/cover-config/route.test.ts` (5), `src/app/api/profile/cover-video/route.test.ts` (3), `src/app/api/posts/media/route.test.ts` (5), `src/app/api/uploads/route.test.ts` (6), `src/app/api/media/process/route.test.ts` (4) and `src/app/api/short-video-covers/route.test.ts` (4). Each imports the handler and calls it with a real `Request`, exactly as Next does; **no HTTP server and no browser are involved** (`next/server` imports and runs under the node environment, `Request`/`FormData`/`File` are Node globals).
- **The harness is a scripted `@/lib/db`, in `src/test/fake-db.ts`, and it deliberately does not answer SQL.** The routes' *results* from drizzle are almost incidental — a role row, one Page row, the row an update returns — while the decisions made from those results are the point. So `FakeDb` is handed the rows a real database would return, keyed by table with `drizzle-orm`'s own `getTableName` (a test scripts against the real exported schema objects, so there is no second table list to drift), consumed in the order the route asks, and it records every read, every `set`/`values` payload and every delete. Two of those records also capture a read's `where` — `selectWheres` (the predicate's SQL) and `selectParams` (its bound values) — which is how a test pins that a list is *gated* rather than merely read; see **What a route test can assert about the fake DB's `where`** below. That record is what lets a test say "the posts were deleted before the Page" and "this write stored `coverUrl` and nothing else", neither of which a mocked return value alone would show. Tables are the key, not a global queue, so `page_roles` then `pages` then `post_media` are scripted independently; a table read twice is answered in order.
- **The other two seams are small.** `@/lib/auth` is reduced to a session that answers `{ user: { id } }` (or `null`), so `requireAuth` in `src/lib/api-helpers.ts` sees a caller without dragging a Supabase client in. `@/lib/r2` is a *partial* mock — `importOriginal` keeps every pure decision real (`replacedObjectUrl`, `keyFromPublicUrl`, `generateKey`, `getPublicUrl`, `validateFile`) while `putObject`, `deleteStoredObjects` and `assertStorageConfigured` become spies; mocking `deleteStoredObjects` is what makes its *argument* assertable, and `assertStorageConfigured` is stubbed only because `src/test/setup.ts` sets the bucket name and public URL but not the account id and keys, so the real one would 503 before the wiring is reached. `withDbRetry` is `(operation) => operation()`: its transient-failure retry is not what these tests are about.
- **What the tests pin, route by route.** Upload: a replaced photo hands `deleteStoredObjects` exactly the old avatar URL, a replaced cover the old cover URL and the cover column is the one written, a first upload offers `[null]` (nothing displaced), a non-admin gets `403` **before `putObject` is called** (the order that stops a rejected upload leaving a file in the bucket), and a non-image is `400` before anything is written. `PUT`: a replaced avatar offers `[oldAvatar, null]`, a **rename with no image fields offers `[null, null]`** — the case a naive `deleteStoredObjects([avatarUrl, coverUrl])` would get wrong by deleting the photo on every rename — clearing the cover offers `[null, oldCover]`, and a non-admin is `403` with nothing read past the role. `DELETE`: the photo, the cover and both post-media URLs are handed over together, `posts` is deleted before `pages`, and a non-admin gets `403` with no delete and no deletion call.
- **Mutations, each run against the final files and `md5sum`-verified back** (`src/app/api/pages/route.ts` `f85d46ace8f687d28983f20557d140db`, `src/app/api/pages/image/route.ts` `632297f096ca7d2e2c796e6de0987e0a`): neutering both `replacedObjectUrl` calls in `PUT` to literal `null` failed **exactly 2** (the replace and clear-cover tests, while the rename test stayed green — the right shape); deleting the non-admin guard in the upload route failed **exactly 1** (the refusal test, which then saw `404` instead of `403`); dropping `...mediaUrls.map(r => r.url)` from the Page delete failed **exactly 1** (the media half of the deletion); and swapping the two deletes to `pages` then `posts` failed **exactly 1** (the ordering assertion). Reverting was done by hand and checked with `md5sum -c` each time — `git checkout` does not work here, because this checkout has no commits (**`HEAD` is unborn and everything is untracked**).
- **Two honest limits.** The fake is keyed by *table*, not by column, so a route that read the wrong column of the same table would not be caught by these tests — which is why the cover test also asserts the written column, the half that is visible. And `deleteStoredObjects` is mocked, so "a storage failure does not fail the upload" is still only a property of that function's own no-throw contract, not something a route test exercises. What the harness does not need is a database, a bucket, or a browser, which is the whole reason it exists.
- **`POST /api/posts` creates a post and its media as two writes, and that pairing is what the tests pin.** One insert writes the row and returns it; only then is `post_media` written from the media list — so the attachments carry the id the *row's own insert* returned and each one's `order` index, which is what the renderer's carousel reads. A test asserts both writes exactly, right down to the returned id and the positions, and that a text-only post writes no media rows at all. The rest pins that the subject is decided by the handler, not the body: publishing as a Page requires a `page_roles` admin row and records `pageId` beside a `authorId` that stays the person (they still own the row); publishing into a group forces `visibility: "group"` whatever the body asks for; and a body naming both a Page and a group is `400`. A body with neither content nor media is `400` before any write. The one seam this needed beyond the others is `@/lib/db/ensure-profile`, mocked to a no-op: the create path calls `ensureLocalUserProfile` best-effort first, and its own read-and-maybe-insert belongs to a provisioning test rather than to one about what the route stores (its `insert(...).onConflictDoNothing(...)` would otherwise run against the fake).
- **`src/app/api/posts/route.test.ts` (13 tests) also pins the post route's storage behaviour, and it found that only one of its three methods has any.** `DELETE /api/posts` is the app's only post-removal path and it *soft*-deletes, which is what makes the cleanup possible: the row stays with `deleted_at` set, so its `post_media` rows survive and are read **after** the update — a hard delete would have to read them first. The tests pin that `deleteStoredObjects` is handed **every** media URL the post owns, that the write is `{ deletedAt }` on `posts` and no row is removed, that a post with no media offers an empty set and still succeeds, and that a post the caller does not own is a `404` that never even queries `post_media` (so no URL reaches a position to be deleted off the back of a request that did not own it).
- **`PUT /api/posts` has no storage wiring at all, and that is the finding rather than a gap in the tests.** Media is deliberately out of scope for an edit — the edit dialog offers text and audience only — so unlike `PUT /api/pages` there is no replacement to clean up. What the route test pins instead is the storage *safety* and the two rules the handler does own: an edit neither reads `post_media` nor calls `deleteStoredObjects` (so a future media-editing change has to say so at this test), a group post's audience stays `group` even when the body asks to widen it to `public`, and a non-author's edit reaches neither the row nor any storage.
- **Mutations, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified** (`src/app/api/posts/route.ts` `b925525faba8d79cc4fdb6bfe169f37c`; `git checkout` does not work here — the checkout has no commits): emptying the media handover to `deleteStoredObjects([])` failed **exactly 1** (the media test, while the no-media one stayed green because an empty set is what it already expects); deleting the group pin (`existing.groupId ? "group" : requestedVisibility`) failed **exactly 1** (the group-audience test); and removing the `if (!deleted) return 404` guard failed **exactly 1** (the ownership test — the non-owner's request then fell through to the media read and a `500` from the missing id, instead of the `404`). Four more covered the create path: using the caller's id instead of `newPost.id` for `post_media.post_id` failed **exactly 1** (the create test, which is the assertion that the media is tied to the row that was just inserted); `order: 0` in place of `order: index` failed **exactly 1** (the same test, on the second attachment's position); dropping the group audience pin failed **exactly 1** (the group test); and writing `pageId: null` in place of `pageForPost` failed **exactly 1** (the Page test).
- **One more limit this fake has, worth knowing before trusting a post-route assertion.** It is keyed by table and does not evaluate a `where`, so the *conditions* the routes write are not what these tests read — an `eq(posts.authorId, …)` dropped from a query would not be caught here. The ownership tests assert the route's *response* to an empty update or select, not the predicate that produced it; the predicates themselves are covered where they are pure (the audience rule in `post-visibility.test.ts`, `authoredByMember` in `author-timeline.test.ts`). The same is true of `deleteStoredObjects` being a spy: "a storage failure does not fail the delete" remains a property of that function's own no-throw contract.
- **The suite total moved under this pass, as it has under every Page pass.** The first full run after the post tests read **1 failed | 401 passed (402)**; the failing file was not captured before the output scrolled, and the next two runs were clean at **402 passed (38 files)** with no change to this work — the same checkout-drift that the earlier note describes, so read any quoted total as a property of the checkout at that moment. `npx tsc --noEmit` held at **51**, and neither new file contributes an error; `npm run build` completed.
- **`src/app/api/posts/comments/route.test.ts` (6 tests) pins the comment write and the total above the list.** `POST` authors the comment as the **session's** user — a body carrying `authorId: "someone-else"` is ignored, which is what the first test asserts by sending one — and keeps a reply's `parentId` while a top-level comment gets `null`; a body missing the post or the content is `400` with nothing written. `DELETE` is a soft delete: the write is `{ deletedAt }` on `comments`, no row is removed, and an update that matched nothing is a `404` (which is how "somebody else's comment" arrives here, since ownership is in the `where`). `GET` is pinned for its envelope, because its `total` is the number the reader sees — a mutation that passed `result.length` instead failed exactly the one test.
- **`src/app/api/posts/reactions/route.test.ts` (6 tests) pins the three-way toggle and the grouped counts.** One press is add, change or remove depending on the row the caller already owns for the target: no row inserts (`userId` from the session, `201`), the same type deletes the row and answers `{reacted:false, type:null}`, a different type updates it and answers the *stored* type. A missing field is `400` with no write. `GET`'s grouping is pure arithmetic over the returned rows, so it is pinned directly: `counts` by type, `total`, and `userReaction` being the caller's own row or `null` — the last one is the counter bug a test catches on its own (reading `result[0]` instead of filtering by the session failed exactly the "has not reacted" test, while the "has reacted" one passed by coincidence because the first row happened to be the same type).
- **The route-coverage ratchet grew a rule mid-pass, and touching it is the intended workflow.** Another session added `rendered-a11y.test.tsx`'s "every api route handler has a test, or is named in `UNTESTED_API`": it discovers `route.ts` handlers and each neighbour `route.test.ts`, and fails on *both* a handler with neither a test nor an allowance **and** an allowance that has since got a test (`stale`). Plainly the point is that the allowlist can only shrink. Adding the two test files made `/api/posts/comments` and `/api/posts/reactions` stale, so their two lines were removed from `UNTESTED_API` — the first edit this work has made to that file, and the minimal one the rule asks for. **Anyone adding a route test here must do the same**, or the suite fails on a route that is now *better* covered.
- **Mutations on the two new routes, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified** (`src/app/api/posts/comments/route.ts` `08860568ec7f6e1b16cc1273c3323aca`, `src/app/api/posts/reactions/route.ts` `b9221af06002172f8f18ba6ef1a8784a`): taking the comment's author from the body failed **exactly 1** (the create test — the body's `authorId` was written); removing the `if (!deleted) return 404` guard failed **exactly 1** (the ownership test, which then saw `200` for a comment it did not own); passing `result.length` as the total failed **exactly 1** (the envelope test); deleting the toggle-off's `db.delete(...)` failed **exactly 1** (the toggle test, whose row was then never removed); writing `existing.type` back on a change failed **exactly 1** (the change test); and reading `result[0]` for `userReaction` failed **exactly 1** (the "has not reacted" test).
- **Totals after this pass:** `npm test -- --run` reads **430 passed / 40 files** (a first run before the allowlist fix read `1 failed | 429 passed`, the failure being the coverage ratchet itself, not a code failure); `npx tsc --noEmit` holds at **51**; `npm run build` completed. The two new files are type-error-free.
- **The four profile media routes had no replacement cleanup, and writing their neighbour tests is what turned that up.** A search for `deleteStoredObjects` or `replacedObjectUrl` under `src/app/api/profile/` returned **nothing**: replacing a profile photo or a cover image overwrote the column and left the previous object in the bucket, saving a Cover Studio config replaced up to 24 photo objects at once with the same result, and removing a cover nulled four columns without removing the photo they named. **All four now read the previous value *before* the write and hand it to `deleteStoredObjects`, exactly as the Page routes do** — see the two implementation bullets below for what each removes, the one deliberate exception (`DELETE /api/profile/cover-video` keeps the published clip as the record of what was published), and the live bucket verification. The neighbour tests were written first and pinned the behavior that existed; the leak was recorded rather than asserted so that a test would not stand in the way of this fix.
- **What the profile tests actually pin.** `POST /api/profile/avatar` stores the photo under the *member's* avatar folder and writes that exact URL to `profiles.avatar_url` (a wrong `getFolderForPurpose` argument fails the one test that checks the folder); a non-image is `400` **before** `putObject`; no session is `401`. `POST /api/profile/cover` writes `cover_url` and validates the type first. `DELETE /api/profile/cover` writes **all four** columns together — dropping any one fails the test, which is the point of the wording "one Remove cover button means all of it". `POST /api/profile/cover-config` stores every photo, resolves `backgroundPhoto` by index with a `null` fallback (removing the `?? null` fails exactly the out-of-range test), writes `coverVideoUrl: null` in the same update so a still cover and a clip cannot both be set (dropping it fails exactly the create test), and refuses an invalid palette before uploading and more than 24 photos with a `400`. `DELETE /api/profile/cover-video` is the one above.
