- **Mutations on the four profile routes, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified** (the `md5`s as they were *before* the cleanup pass below: `avatar` `84005d08f490897a7cdf5b246fa87fa6`, `cover` `f576c79a72d9b8b31abb77def47e5b85`, `cover-config` `babc85cc237aab171d607e24cccb7f43`, `cover-video` `ed8138d4586c859e7261cabff7ab2466`): pointing the avatar's key at the `cover` folder failed **exactly 1**; dropping `shortVideoCoverConfig: null` from the cover removal failed **exactly 1**; dropping `coverVideoUrl: null` from a config save failed **exactly 1**; removing the `?? null` from `backgroundPhoto` failed **exactly 1** (the out-of-range test); and adding `coverUrl: null` to the cover-video removal — the mutation that silently deletes a member's still cover with their clip — failed **exactly 1**.
- **A concurrent session was editing the coverage ratchet while these files were written, which is worth knowing before touching it again.** `rendered-a11y.test.tsx`'s `UNTESTED_API` changed underfoot mid-pass: the `/api/profile/avatar`, `/api/profile/cover` and `/api/profile/cover-config` entries disappeared (and then `/api/profile/cover-video`) as the new neighbour tests appeared, so no edit from this pass was needed in the end. It is the same ratchet described above — **a route test added here makes the matching `UNTESTED_API` entry stale and the suite fails until it is removed** — and with two sessions on the same tree the only safe move is to re-read that block before editing it rather than to write a removal that is already gone.
- **Implemented: `POST /api/profile/avatar`, `POST /api/profile/cover`, `POST /api/profile/cover-config` and `DELETE /api/profile/cover` now remove the objects they displace.** Each reads the previous value **before** the write — after it, the old URL is recorded nowhere — and hands it to `replacedObjectUrl`/`deleteStoredObjects`. Avatar and cover each remove the one image they replace, and only when the row was actually written: the avatar route's deferred-database path leaves the old URL as the one the profile points at, so `displaced` stays null there and its object is **not** removed. Cover-config removes every photo the **replaced** config held (a save with no new photos still replaces the old config, which is also how a photo-only animated cover is cleared), and the cover removal removes the still photo plus the config's photos. `deleteStoredObjects` filters to our own public URLs and swallows failures, so a storage hiccup cannot fail a request the row already records. The photo list is read with a new pure helper, `coverConfigPhotoUrls` in `src/lib/cover-config.ts`, defensive over the untyped `cover_config` JSONB the same way `parseCoverVideoConfig` is over `shortVideoCoverConfig` (its own 4 tests).
- **The published cover video's object is deliberately *not* removed on either cover path.** `DELETE /api/profile/cover-video` keeps the clip as the record of what was published, so deleting it from `DELETE /api/profile/cover` or from a config save (which only sets `coverVideoUrl: null`) would make "Remove cover" destroy history that "Remove video" preserves. That is the one stated retention, and it is why this route's neighbour test asserts the field write and not just the URL list. **`DELETE /api/profile/cover-video` itself is unchanged** — it was already the deliberate exception, not a leak.
- **Mutations on the new cleanup, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified** (current `md5`s: `avatar` `2960211cff9cafa90d1a6947cb8a8970`, `cover` `ad9b984a5ba4a65afd0393d8629e75fa`, `cover-config` `ec1709e99adc645c4dea360626358b66`, `src/lib/cover-config.ts` `a718d1f7121a29ba957681faa6e364fe`): making the avatar's `displaced` always `null` failed **exactly 1** (the replace test, while the empty-column test stayed green); passing `[null]` instead of `replacedObjectUrl(current?.coverUrl, coverUrl)` on a cover upload failed **exactly 1**; dropping `...coverConfigPhotoUrls(current?.coverConfig)` from the cover removal failed **exactly 1**; and passing `[]` instead of `coverConfigPhotoUrls(current?.coverConfig)` on a config save failed **exactly 1** (the replaced-config test, while the first-config test's `[]` assertion stayed green).
- **Verified live against the running dev server and the real bucket, on a truly clean target — the signed-in member's `cover_url`, `cover_config` and `cover_video_url` were all `null`, so every probe started and ended at nothing and no real object was at risk** (`avatar_url` holds a real object, so it was verified separately — see the next bullet). Cover-config: save a probe photo → `curl` it `200`; save a second → the first is **`404`**, the second `200`; save a config with no photos → the second is **`404`**. Cover: upload → `200`; upload again → the first `404`, the second `200`; `DELETE /api/profile/cover` → the second **`404`**. The server logged exactly the four expected lines (`Deleted 1 replaced cover photo(s)`, twice, then `Deleted 1 replaced cover object(s)` and `Deleted 1 cover object(s)`), and `avatar_url` was still `200` at the end — untouched. The profile's five media columns were read back and matched the pre-test snapshot exactly (`cover_url`/`cover_config`/`cover_video_url`/`short_video_cover_config` all `null`, the same avatar). The snapshot/restore helper is `.freebuff/profile-probe.mjs` (`show <username>`, `restore-config`, `restore-video`, `restore-cover`, `restore-avatar`, and `delete-key`, which removes one R2 object directly); restoring `cover_config` to `null` was the only direct database write the cover check needed, because the routes themselves deleted every object they uploaded.
- **The avatar route was verified live too, with disposable probes, and the real avatar was never at risk.** Its `avatar_url` held a real object, so the check first **detached** it — the column was set to `null` directly (a database write, not a storage one), which left the real object untouched and still `200`, and meant no probe could ever be the one the route deleted. Then two probe avatars were uploaded through `POST /api/profile/avatar`: the first replaced an empty column (nothing deleted), the second replaced the first, and `curl` confirmed the first was **`404`** while the second was `200` and the real avatar was **still `200`**. The server logged `Deleted 1 replaced profile photo(s)`. Restoring was a direct `restore-avatar` back to the original URL plus a `delete-key` for the last probe (the one object no route could reach), after which the real avatar was `200`, both probes were `404`, and the profile's five columns matched the pre-test snapshot exactly. This also exercises the route's ordinary path; the deferred-database branch (no deletion) is the one the tests pin, since it needs a database timeout.
- **The avatar route's deferred-database branch is pinned in the same file (it is now 6 tests).** When the profile write cannot be made, the route defers the URL to Supabase auth metadata instead of failing an upload R2 already accepted — and on that path the row still points at the old URL, so **its object must not be removed**, which is exactly the ordinary path's read-before-write ordering turned into a condition. The test makes the write reject (through a new `failNextUpdate(table, error)` seam on `src/test/fake-db.ts`, the first way the fake can fail an operation), scripts a previous avatar, and asserts the response is still `200`, `deleteStoredObjects` was **not** called, no `profiles` write was recorded, and `supabase.auth.updateUser` was. A second test makes that metadata write fail too and asserts a `500` with, again, nothing removed — the one case where both places the photo could be attached failed, and the old photo is still what the member is shown on reload until one of them succeeds. Mutations: moving `displaced = replacedObjectUrl(...)` **above** the update (so a failed write still offers the old URL up) failed **exactly 1** — the deferred test — while the ordinary replace test stayed green; and swallowing `metadataError` (so a doubly-failed write answers `200`) failed **exactly 1** — the second test. Reverted, `md5sum -c`-verified (`src/app/api/profile/avatar/route.ts` `2960211cff9cafa90d1a6947cb8a8970`).
- **Audit: the storage-using routes that had no test, and the failure paths around a write.** Ten of the 39 routes touch storage; five of those (the Page, post, and profile ones) already had tests. The other four — `posts/media`, `uploads`, `media/process`, `short-video-covers` — had none, so every storage failure they can produce was only ever seen live. Each now has a neighbour test, and each pins the failure the request asked about:
  - **`posts/media`** (5): a missing file and a disallowed type are `400` before storage; **unconfigured** storage is a `503` with the configuration message; a `putObject` that **fails** is a `500` with **no `url`** in the body — a client that recorded one would store a dead attachment, the same reason a `blob:` URL is never persisted.
  - **`uploads`** (6): the presigned route is unused by the browser now (the bucket sends no CORS headers) but still serves anything outside one, so it must not sign what it cannot: type and size are validated first, unconfigured storage is `503`, and a signing failure is `500` with no `uploadUrl`.
  - **`media/process`** (4): a key that names **no object** is its own `404 File not found` rather than the generic `500` an SDK error gives — the only place the route draws that line — and a `send` that fails writes nothing.
  - **`short-video-covers`** (4): see the next bullet.
- **The one deliberately swallowed write, now pinned.** `POST /api/short-video-covers` does two writes of different importance: the **profile** update is the publish (sets `coverVideoUrl`, clears `coverConfig`), and the **`short_video_covers` insert** is history, wrapped in a `catch` that logs and continues "so a schema that has not caught up with the migration must not take an otherwise-published cover down with it." That asymmetry had no test. The test makes the history insert fail and asserts the request still answers **`201` with `coverId: null`** while the profile was really written — and a second test makes an *upload* fail and asserts the opposite: `response.ok` false with **no profile write**, because the banner must not switch to a clip that was never stored. This needed a new fake-db seam, `failNextInsert(table, error)`, the insert counterpart of `failNextUpdate`; a rejected insert is likewise not recorded as a write. **A finding worth carrying forward:** that route's outer catch answers `errorResponse(err.message)` with no status, so a storage failure during publish is a **`400`, not a `500`** — the tests assert `response.ok === false` rather than cementing the number, and it is a candidate for a small fix.
- **Mutations on the four audited routes, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified** (`posts/media` `8c1b3b1a9f86dca7e978e2ac5d890bda`, `uploads` `5fd27cbe7b463fc1c8b9b608bc270f6d`, `media/process` `40e21c7f800168b075f10c580b153cf9`, `short-video-covers` `7594431f2e2dac9dc8b0678aa43c8e08`): changing the unconfigured-storage status to `500` failed **exactly 1** in `posts/media`; the same in `uploads` failed **exactly 1**; making the missing-object `404` a `500` failed **exactly 1** in `media/process`; and making the swallowed history-insert `catch` rethrow failed **exactly 1** in `short-video-covers` (the publish test). Four routes, four paths, one failure each.
- **The coverage ratchet was updated with them**: `/api/posts/media`, `/api/uploads`, `/api/media/process` and `/api/short-video-covers` were removed from `UNTESTED_API`, since a neighbour test now sits beside each handler. As everywhere else, adding the test without removing the entry would fail the ratchet on a route that is now *better* covered.
- **The write-heavy marketplace, jobs and groups routes now have neighbour tests, and each pins the order of its writes and the failure that stops them.** These are the three routes with the most writes per request, so the tests are about *sequence* and *halting*: `src/app/api/groups/route.test.ts` (7), `src/app/api/marketplace/route.test.ts` (7) and `src/app/api/jobs/route.test.ts` (7).
  - **`groups`** (7): creating a group is **two** writes — the `groups` row, then the creator's `group_members` row with `role: "admin"`, keyed by the id the first insert returned — and the test pins that pair and their order, which is why the insert has to come first. A missing name or a `visibility` the schema does not allow is a `400` with nothing written; a **failed** group insert is a `500` with no membership left pointing at a group that does not exist. Editing and deleting are gated on an admin read of `group_members`, so an empty role read is the `403` a stranger meets, and an admin delete lands on `groups` (the route reaches no storage: a group's cover is a URL on the row, not an uploaded object).
  - **`marketplace`** (7): creating a listing is up to **four** writes — the listing, then `listing_media`, `product_variants` and `inventory_items`, every child keyed by the id the first insert returned — and the test pins the whole set *in order*, with the listing created as a `draft` (what keeps an incomplete listing out of `GET`'s `status = 'active'` read). A listing with no title is a `400`; a failed listing insert is a `500` with **no child rows attempted**. Editing and deleting compare against `seller_id`, so a stranger's request matches no row and is a `404` — and the delete is a **soft** delete (`{ status: "removed", deletedAt }`), not a removed row, which is why the ownership test is an update that matched nothing rather than a delete that found nothing.
  - **`jobs`** (7): `POST` checks the company exists (`404` when it does not) and records the posting as `status: "active"` straight away; a missing company or title is a `400` before any write. `PUT` requires an id and writes **only the fields the request carried** (an unmentioned column is absent from the write, so a partial update cannot blank a field it was not asked about). `DELETE` **archives** (`{ status: "archived" }`) rather than removing the row, and both `PUT` and `DELETE` are a `404` when no row matched.
- **Two findings recorded rather than asserted, so the tests do not cement a gap.** **(1)** `jobs` has **no ownership or company-admin check**: `marketplaceListings` filters on `seller_id` and `groups` on an admin `group_members` row, but `jobs` `PUT`/`DELETE` filter on the id alone and `POST` never checks that the caller administers the company — so any signed-in member can edit or archive any posting. **(2)** `groups` does **not** recover from a failure between its two writes: the group is inserted before the membership, so a failure on the second insert would leave a group nobody administers (the write-failure test deliberately stops at the *first* insert). Both are written into the test-file headers and left as fix candidates; pinning them would make today's behaviour look intended.

Four paths, one failure each.

## Reading a job's applications is now company-admin-only

- **The last recorded finding on `GET /api/jobs/applications` is closed, and the route's `md5` has changed again** (`c368e961c02535f6d3a70c82a29365fc` → `495435e161d220694cdb63ac14d898d8`). The list of who applied to a job is that company's own hiring information, so reading it is now scoped exactly like deciding it: the request reads the job (`404 Job not found` when it names nothing), reads its company, and refuses a caller who is not an admin of the company's Page with `403 Only a company admin can view applications` — **before** `job_applications` is read at all. A company with a **null** `page_id` has no admin, so nobody can read its applications: the same deliberate limit the `jobs` route and this route's `PUT` already enforce.
- **The admin edge is now one shared helper rather than two copies.** The `jobs` route's company-admin check lived inside `adminsJobsCompany`; it is split so the Page-role test is its own function, `adminsCompanyPage(userId, pageId)` (null Page → `false` immediately, without reading `page_roles`), and `adminsJobsCompany` (used by `PUT`) now just reads the job and its company and hands the `page_id` to it. `GET` reads the job and company itself — it needs the `404` and the company row anyway — and calls the same helper. Both refusal paths therefore reach one implementation of "is this person an admin of this Page", which is the point.
- **`src/app/api/jobs/applications/route.test.ts` is now 15 tests** (was 12). The `PUT` tests are unchanged (the reads they script are still job → company → `page_roles`). New `GET` cases: the missing-job `404` (asserting neither `companies` nor `job_applications` was read), the non-admin `403` (asserting `job_applications` was never read), the null-Page `403` (asserting `page_roles` and `job_applications` were never read), and the page-envelope test re-scripted to put a company admin in front of the two `job_applications` reads.
- **Mutations on the GET scoping, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified** (`src/app/api/jobs/applications/route.ts` `495435e161d220694cdb63ac14d898d8`): removing the whole GET admin guard failed **exactly 2** (the non-admin and null-Page `GET` tests — the right shape for a guard that covers both); removing the missing-job `404` failed **exactly 1** (the `404` test, which then read `job.companyId` off `undefined` and got a `500`); making the shared page helper ignore the role row (`return true`) failed **exactly 2** (the `PUT` *and* `GET` non-admin tests, confirming the one helper serves both); and dropping the null-Page short-circuit so `page_roles` is queried with a null `pageId` failed **exactly 2** (both null-Page tests, on their `page_roles`-never-read assertion).

## Marketplace inventory is now the seller's alone

- **`/api/marketplace/inventory` had no ownership check at all, and that is the finding this pass closes.** A listing's stock belongs to the listing's **seller** — `inventory_items` names a listing and `marketplace_listings.seller_id` names its owner — yet `GET` returned any listing's inventory and its movement history to any signed-in member, and `POST` let anyone move anyone's stock (adjust the quantity and write an `inventory_movements` row attributed to themselves). Both methods are now scoped to the seller, the same `seller_id` edge `src/app/api/marketplace/route.ts` already uses for its own writes.
- **The route's `md5` has changed** (`33857746bb5cb4e291fc631068bbc29b` → `ca941b1fab856e4a42434cd8c26cea31`). `GET` reads the listing (`404 Listing not found` when it is not there), refuses a caller who is not its seller with `403 Only the seller can view this inventory`, and only then reads the stock and its movements. `POST` reads the inventory row (`404` if it is gone) and then the listing, refusing a stranger with `403 Only the seller can adjust this inventory` **before** the quantity update and the movement insert. The sibling marketplace route answers a stranger `404` (`Listing not found or unauthorized`) instead; the `403` here is a deliberate choice — a listing is public (`GET /api/marketplace?id=…` needs no ownership), so its existence is not a secret, and naming the refusal is the clearer answer.
- **`src/app/api/marketplace/inventory/route.test.ts` (11 tests) is new.** `GET`: a missing `listingId` is `400` before any read; a listing that is not there is `404` with no stock read; a non-seller is `403` with neither the stock nor its movements read; the seller's listing with no inventory row is `404`; and the seller gets `{inventory, movements}` with the reads in order (`marketplace_listings` → `inventory_items` → `inventory_movements`). `POST`: missing fields are `400` before any read; a missing inventory row is `404` with no listing read and no write; a non-owner is `403` with **no write**; and the successful movements pin the two writes in order — `inventory_items` `{quantity}` first, then `inventory_movements` with `actorId` from the **session** — for an `added` (increment), a `sold` (decrement) and an `adjusted` (absolute).
- **Mutations, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified** (`src/app/api/marketplace/inventory/route.ts` `ca941b1fab856e4a42434cd8c26cea31`): removing the `GET` seller check failed **exactly 1** (the non-seller `GET` test, which then saw the empty stock read as a `404`); removing the `POST` seller check failed **exactly 1** (the non-owner `POST` test, which then reached the writes and got a `201`); making `adjusted` an increment instead of an absolute set failed **exactly 1** (the adjustment test); and removing the `GET` missing-listing `404` failed **exactly 1** (the not-found test, which then threw on `listing.sellerId` and got a `500`).
- **A pre-existing type error, recorded rather than fixed (it is not this pass's).** `npx tsc --noEmit` reports `src/app/api/marketplace/inventory/route.ts(100,9): error TS18047: 'newQuantity' is possibly 'null'` — `inventory_items.quantity` is nullable in the schema, so `let newQuantity = inventory.quantity` is `number | null` and the `+=` branches are flagged. It was in the file before this pass and the total error count is unchanged at **51**, so this work neither added nor removed one. It is a real latent bug (a null quantity would compute `NaN`), left as a fix candidate rather than folded into a scoping change.
- **The coverage ratchet was updated with it**: `/api/marketplace/inventory` was removed from `UNTESTED_API`, so `/api/groups/members` is now the last of the `groups`/`jobs`/`marketplace` sub-routes still named there.
- **Totals after the inventory scoping:** `npm test -- --run` reads **653 passed / 62 files**; `npm run build` completed; `npx tsc --noEmit` holds at **51**. Read every count as a property of the checkout at that moment.

## Zero type errors, and a real lint gate

- **`npx tsc --noEmit` reads 0, down from the 51 this runbook recorded pass after pass.** Two causes, in order of size. First, the repository had **no `@types/node`**, so every `process`, `Buffer` and `fs` reference typed as an error; adding it as a devDependency (`@types/node@^24.19.0`) dropped the count **51 → 15** on its own. Second, the remaining errors were all Cloudflare **worker** globals (`Env`, `ExecutionContext`, `DurableObjectState`/`Namespace`/`Stub`, `Fetcher`, `KVNamespace`, `R2Bucket`, `Queue`, `WebSocketPair`, `WebSocket.accept`, `ResponseInit.webSocket`) that nothing installed provided.
- **The install needs `--legacy-peer-deps`, the same pre-existing `ERESOLVE` the jsdom note describes.** `package.json` pins `@cloudflare/workers-types` `^4` while `wrangler@4.135.0` carries a peerOptional on `^5`, so plain `npm install` aborts. `npm install --save-dev @types/node@^24 --legacy-peer-deps` succeeds and is additive; `npm ci` (no flag) is clean afterwards and the lockfile records `@types/node: ^24.19.0`.
- **The worker globals are hand-written, deliberately, and that is the whole point of the section.** The obvious fix — a `/// <reference types="@cloudflare/workers-types" />`, or a full `npx wrangler types` — emits a ~601 KB file that redeclares `Response`, `Request`, `WebSocket`, `Element` and `ParentNode`, colliding with the `lib.dom` this Next app also typechecks: applied, it produces **387 errors**, because every `res.json()` becomes `unknown` and DOM nodes stop matching their own interfaces. So `worker-globals.d.ts` (89 lines, LF, committed, not gitignored) declares just the names the app uses and, where it must extend a DOM type, **merges** into it (`interface WebSocket { accept(): void }`, `interface ResponseInit { webSocket?: WebSocket | null }`) rather than redeclaring it, so the DOM types survive intact.
- **The `Env` bindings are generated, not guessed.** `worker-configuration.d.ts` (29 lines) comes from `npx wrangler types --include-runtime false` — **the `--include-runtime false` is the trick**: it emits the binding interfaces (`CACHE`, `UPLOADS`, `JOB_QUEUE`, `ASSETS`, `DATABASE_URL`, the R2 keys, `WEBSOCKET_ROOM`, `AI`, …) without the runtime globals that cause the 387-error collision above. It is kept as the `npm run types:worker` script; regenerate it when `wrangler.toml`'s bindings change, and do not run the bare command.
- **Three errors were real code, not missing types, and were fixed rather than suppressed.** `src/hooks/use-websocket.ts` destructured `const { data: session }` from `useSession()`, which returns `{ session, loading, user }` — now `const { session }`. `src/app/api/marketplace/inventory/route.ts` now reads `let newQuantity = inventory.quantity ?? 0`, which closes the nullable-quantity latent bug the **Marketplace inventory** section above recorded but left unfixed (a null quantity would have computed `NaN`). And `src/lib/r2.ts`'s `putObject` now normalizes an `ArrayBuffer` body to `new Uint8Array(body)`, because S3's `PutObjectCommand` takes `Uint8Array | string`, never a raw `ArrayBuffer`.
- **`vinext.config.ts` was deleted.** It called `defineConfig` from `vinext/config`, a subpath the installed `vinext` does not export, so it could only ever throw; nothing in the repository imported it, and the real build config is `vite.config.ts` (which wires `vinext()` and `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`).
- **The same pass turned `npm run lint` from "cannot run" into a real gate, because the clean typecheck could not be reached in CI without it.** The lint job runs `npm run lint` *before* `npm run typecheck`, and with no ESLint installed `next lint` opened its interactive setup prompt and exited 1 under no TTY — so a passing typecheck never got a turn. `eslint` and `eslint-config-next` (both `^15`/`^9`, matching Next 15) are now devDependencies, the script is `eslint .`, and `eslint.config.mjs` bridges Next's eslintrc-style shareable configs (`next/core-web-vitals`, `next/typescript`) through `FlatCompat` from `@eslint/eslintrc`, ignoring `.next`, `.vinext`, `.wrangler`, `dist`, `next-env.d.ts` and the generated `worker-configuration.d.ts`. Install needed `--legacy-peer-deps` like every other install here.
- **The first run found 33 errors, and the fixes split into "correct it" and "configure it deliberately".** Corrected outright: three `prefer-const` locals (auto-fixed) plus a fourth `dy` in `short-video-canvas.tsx` that could not auto-fix because it shared a `let` with reassigned siblings (split out as `const dy = 0`); a `//` line-comment sitting inside JSX children in `authenticator-security.tsx`, which was both the `react/jsx-no-comment-textnodes` error *and* the source of a `no-unescaped-entities` error on the apostrophe in that comment (now a `{/* … */}` block); an unescaped `'` in `profile-qr-card.tsx` (`&apos;`); the two `const module` locals in `rendered-a11y.test.tsx`, which shadowed Node's `module` and tripped `@next/next/no-assign-module-variable` (renamed `mod`); and `useTransactionPooler` in `src/lib/db/index.ts`, a plain function whose `use` prefix made `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` fire (renamed `applyTransactionPooler`, both references). One `@typescript-eslint/no-this-alias` in `src/test/dom-leaks.ts` — the deliberate capture of the `EventTarget` an `addEventListener` wrapper must remember — is an inline disable with the reason on the line above.
- **The `no-explicit-any` sites were then typed properly and the rule put back to `error`.** Each was replaced in the shape the data actually has rather than suppressed: `unknown` for the generic JSON responders (`api-helpers.ts`); Supabase's `Session`/`User` for the auth client, with a named `AuthUser` intersection carrying the `name`/`username`/`image` fields the app reads off the account that Supabase's `User` does not declare; one small input interface per request body (`ProfileUpdateBody` with the visibility enum from `visibilityEnum.enumValues`, `ListingMediaInput`, `ProductVariantInput`, `PostMediaInput`, `ConversationPayload`); the `RoomMessage`/`WebSocketMessage` message shapes (index signature `unknown`, not `any`); the reports filter typed from `reportStatusEnum.enumValues` with the `status as any` gone; and a declared global for the `vinext` fetch shim instead of `(globalThis as any)`. Two websocket consumers had to narrow (`typeof userId !== "string"`) once the index signature stopped being `any` — which is the point. `eslint.config.mjs` now sets `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` to `"error"`.
- **The 98 remaining `no-unused-vars` warnings were almost all dead imports, and were deleted rather than configured away.** Only `_`-prefixed names are ignored (`argsIgnorePattern`, `varsIgnorePattern`, `caughtErrorsIgnorePattern`, `destructuredArrayIgnorePattern`, all `^_`); everything else the rule named was genuinely unused — roughly ninety import specifiers across some forty-five files (`Card`/`CardHeader`/`CardTitle`, dozens of `lucide-react` glyphs, drizzle operators like `sql`/`and`/`storefronts`, an unused `session` destructured from `requireAuth`, unused schema imports in tests), a handful of dead locals (the `const people` array on the landing page, unused refs and `const`s in `short-video-canvas.tsx`, an unused `world` in an integration test), and unused parameters renamed `_`-prefixed rather than deleted so call sites do not move (`_request` in `requireAuth`, `_purpose` in `validateFile`, `_input`, `_size`, `_targetUserId`, `_env`/`_ctx` in both workers).
- **A few non-`any` findings were fixed too.** The three anonymous default exports (`postcss.config.mjs`, `src/index.ts`, `worker/index.ts`) now assign to a named `const` before exporting; and `profile-header.tsx`'s section nav carried `aria-selected` on a plain `<button>`, which `jsx-a11y/role-supports-aria-props` correctly rejects — it is a nav, not a tablist, so the selected state stays on `aria-current="page"` alone.
- **That last 26-warning backlog — 18 `no-img-element`, 8 `exhaustive-deps` — was then cleared, and the two rule families were handled differently on purpose.** `@next/next/no-img-element` is now **off in `eslint.config.mjs`**, with the reason written beside it. Reading vinext's `next/image` shim (`node_modules/vinext/dist/shims/image.js`) settled what converting actually does: it only routes *local* sources (starting with `/`) through the Cloudflare Images optimizer, and this app has no `public/` directory; a remote URL matching `images.remotePatterns` renders as a plain `<img>` under `fill` and through `@unpic/react` under width/height, and `*.r2.dev` is not a transform-capable CDN, so neither is optimized; a remote URL that *doesn't* match makes the shim `return null` in production, so the image disappears (seeded content stores arbitrary external URLs, which no allowlist can cover); and `blob:`/`data:` previews (file-upload and post-composer object URLs, Cover Studio's canvas, the TOTP QR code) are not treated as remote, so they would be sent to `/_next/image`, which rejects a url that does not start with `/`. `next.config.mjs` was corrected to list the real R2 public host — `**.r2.dev`, plus the `R2_PUBLIC_URL` host when set at build time; the old `**.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` entry was the S3 API endpoint, which never serves a public object — so a future `next/image` use is allowed, but converting today would change nothing visually while risking blank images. `MediaImage` stays a deliberate `<img>` with its own fallback. The 8 `exhaustive-deps` warnings were real and are fixed by giving each effect the value it actually reads: `fetchPosts` added to `feed/page.tsx`'s `focusPost`; `messages/page.tsx` keyed on a scalar `selectedConversationId` rather than the whole conversation object; `profile/page.tsx` listing the primitive `authMetadata.*`/`user.email` fallbacks (compared by value, so a re-render that changed nothing cannot re-run it); `settings/page.tsx` adding the session-stable `user.user_metadata`; both auth components memoising the Supabase client, since `createClient()` rebuilt it every render and a raw dep would loop (`authenticator-security.tsx`'s `loadFactor` is also wrapped in `useCallback`); `use-file-upload.ts`'s `uploadFile` wrapped in `useCallback` so `uploadAll` can depend on it; and one justified `eslint-disable-next-line` in `virtual-feed-list.tsx`, where `measureTick` is a deliberate invalidation signal for heights held in a ref. A backstop now guards all of it: `src/test/lint-baseline.test.ts` runs ESLint programmatically over the project (the same config `npm run lint` uses) and fails on a single error *or* warning — plain `npm run lint` cannot, because warnings do not fail it — and separately asserts `eslint.config.mjs` still sets `@next/next/no-img-element` to `"off"` with the reason written beside it, so re-enabling the rule is caught even if every `<img>` were converted. The same file also guards the other way a finding can vanish — silencing it. It scans `src` and `worker` for `eslint-disable`/`-next-line`/`-line` directives, requires a comment on the line above each, and compares the set against a short `DISABLE_ALLOWLIST` keyed by file and rule; a new suppression fails until it is recorded there with a reason phrase that must still appear above the directive. The two allowed today are `virtual-feed-list.tsx`'s `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` (its `measureTick` invalidation signal) and `dom-leaks.ts`'s `@typescript-eslint/no-this-alias` (the captured event target); a probe confirmed an undocumented third one fails both the set check and the reason check.
- **CI now fails on a warning too, so the zero-warning baseline is enforced outside the test suite.** `npm run lint` stays permissive by design (warnings are still useful while iterating locally), so the gate lives in a separate `lint:ci` script — `eslint . --max-warnings 0` — and the workflow's lint job runs `npm run lint:ci` *before* `npm run typecheck`. `--max-warnings 0` makes ESLint exit non-zero on a single warning, so a re-introduced `exhaustive-deps` or `no-unused-vars` warning fails the job the same way an error does; the vitest backstop above remains the local, off-CI guard. Verified by seeding one unused binding (exit 1, `0 errors, 1 warning`), then removing it. The same test file now also holds the **typecheck baseline**: its last block runs the compiler the script does (`node_modules/typescript/lib/tsc.js --noEmit --pretty false --incremental false`, spawned via `process.execPath` rather than the `.bin` shim) and fails on any `error TS\d+` diagnostic, so a local `npm test` can no longer pass over a file that no longer typechecks. `--incremental false` forces a full check instead of trusting a `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` that may predate the tree, and `--pretty false` keeps each diagnostic on one parseable line. Verified by seeding a `const x: number = "…"` (reported `TS2322`), then removing it.
- **The lint gate is a CI stage of its own now, so a reintroduced warning is named in one line instead of buried in the suite's report.** `.freebuff/lint-baseline.mjs` (`npm run lint:baseline`) runs the same whole-project ESLint the scripts do and fails on any finding, error or warning — the `lint:ci` command as a tool rather than a script alias. `.freebuff/ci.mjs`'s new `lint` stage (ordered third, after `runbook` and before the suite, since it is read-only and seconds long) reads its `--json` contract — `{ gate, files, findings[], errors, warnings }`, each finding carrying its project-relative `file`, `line`, `column`, `rule` and `message` — and prints `N file(s), no findings` or names each finding by `file:line:column` with its rule, the failing line rather than the whole ESLint report. It is a JSON gate alongside `runbook`, `preflight` and `mutation`; the seam `CI_LINT_SCRIPT` stubs it in `src/test/ci-runner.test.ts`, which covers a clean project, a payload that names each finding with its rule and severity, and a crash that writes no JSON (which fails rather than passing). The fuller baseline — the `eslint-disable` allowlist and the written reason for `@next/next/no-img-element` being off — stays in `src/test/lint-baseline.test.ts`, because a stage reads ESLint's findings and cannot see a config decision or a suppression.
- **The suite now carries a line-coverage floor, so a module can no longer land with no test at all.** `@vitest/coverage-v8` is a devDependency, `vitest.config.ts` collects v8 coverage over `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` with `all: true` (a source file no test imports is reported at 0%, which is the point) and excludes test files and the `src/test/**` harness, and `thresholds` now hold **per directory** (see the next bullet) over a bare global backstop of lines/statements **64**, branches **67**, functions **47** (later tightened to 72/72/69/51 — see below). A new `test:coverage` script is `vitest run --coverage`, and the CI **Test** job runs that instead of `npm test -- --run`, so a dropped floor fails the job; local `npm test` stays fast and coverage-free. Note this is a *global* floor, distinct from the `UNTESTED_API` **route-coverage ratchet** elsewhere in this file (that one is about a neighbour `route.test.ts`, not lines). `.coverage/` is gitignored. Verified three ways: the full suite passes the thresholds (64.74 / 67.75 / 47.36); a deliberately small run (`vitest run src/lib/r2.test.ts --coverage`) exits 1 with `Coverage for lines (0.38%) does not meet global threshold (64%)`; and a seeded 215-line untested module (`src/lib/__coverage_probe.ts`, since deleted) pulled lines to 63.96% and failed the floor with every test still green.
- **Every source file the floor measures is now covered, so a per-file threshold has become possible.** When the floor was added, 16 included files sat at 0%; the suite now has **0 of 168**. Fifteen got tests — `src/lib/publish-post`, `src/lib/image-processing`, `src/lib/weak-ref-polyfill`, `src/lib/db/demo-media`, `src/lib/db/index`(the `withDbRetry` ladder), `src/index` (the vinext fetch shim), `src/middleware`, `src/utils/supabase/server`, `src/utils/supabase/middleware`, `src/hooks/use-file-upload`, `src/components/auth-provider`, `src/components/providers/notification-provider`, both layouts, and the `WebSocketRoom` Durable Object — and the sixteenth, `src/lib/db/seed.ts`, is **excluded** from coverage because it is an operational script (`npm run db:seed`): it runs on import and ends the pool, so it cannot be driven in-process. `src/lib/weak-ref-polyfill.ts` gained an `export {}` so its side-effect-only import is a module. That pass moved the totals from 64.7/67.8/47.4 to **73.0 lines / 70.5 branches / 52.3 functions**. The lowest included file is now `src/lib/auth.ts` at 12.9% lines; 156 of 168 are at or above 50%. A per-file *line* floor around 10% is therefore viable now, though Vitest has no separate global-vs-per-file number (its `perFile` flag re-applies the same numbers to every file).
- **The floor is per directory now, not one global number.** Vitest checks a glob-keyed threshold against the *combined* coverage of the files it matches (and still checks the bare numbers against every file), so `vitest.config.ts` holds each area to what it actually sustains (the numbers were later moved to `.freebuff/coverage-thresholds.mjs` — see the report bullet below): **`src/lib/**` 88/86/58**, **`src/utils/**` 98/99/85**, **`src/hooks/**` 77/73/71**, **`src/app/**` 77/68/57**, **`src/components/**` 63/63/41** (lines/branches/functions; measured aggregates are 88.5/86.8/58.6, 98.6/100/85.7, 77.4/73.3/71.4, 77.8/68.8/57.2 and 63.7/64.0/41.9). Each sits a point or two under today's number, and the ordering states a fact rather than a preference: `src/lib` and `src/utils` are pure logic and are held high, while `src/components` — presentational and the costliest to mount — is held lowest. The bare global is a whole-tree backstop for files no glob names (`src/index.ts`, `src/middleware.ts`, and anything new at the root of `src/`), and it was then **tightened from 64/67/47 to 72/72/69/51** — a shade under today's 72.97 / 70.5 / 52.32 lines/branches/functions. Held at the old numbers it was decorative next to the globs: a directory could bleed several points before the aggregate spoke up. Verified: the full suite passes all of them; a seeded 40-line untested module under `src/lib` (`src/lib/__dir_probe.ts`, since deleted) dropped that directory to **86.59%** and failed with `Coverage for lines (86.59%) does not meet "src/lib/**" threshold (88%)`; and, for the tightened backstop, a seeded untested module at the root of `src/` (`src/__global_probe.ts`, since deleted) pulled the whole tree to **71.87%** and failed with `Coverage for lines (71.87%) does not meet global threshold (72%)` while all 1078 tests stayed green. Both probes are gone and the run is back to exit 0.
- **The twelve files still under 50% lines were brought above it, so a per-file floor became possible.** The directory aggregates could not see these individually — each was a single file averaged against better-covered neighbours — and they were the whole reason a per-file floor was not yet enforceable. Each got a test of its own: `src/lib/auth.ts` (the server auth facade, driven with a fake Supabase client through every helper and `requireAuth`'s 401) and `src/lib/auth-client.ts` (the session hooks plus every sign-in/sign-out helper) both reached **100%**; `src/components/realtime/typing-indicator.tsx` (**100%**) drives the fake websocket through one/two/several, a duplicate, a stop-typing, a message, a wrong-conversation and a wrong-typed message, plus the stale sweep on fake timers; `src/components/ui/file-upload.tsx` (**99.5%**) covers choosing, dropping, the slot limit, removal and both upload steps with each failure shape; `src/components/profile/profile-avatar-upload.tsx` and `profile-details-card.tsx` (**100%**) cover the validation ladder and each conditional row; `src/components/profile/member-list-dialog.tsx` (**100%**) covers load/empty/error, pagination with dedup, and the live add/remove paths (via a stubbed `FollowButton`); the two canvas components needed a harness — `src/test/canvas.ts` installs a no-op `Proxy` 2D context, an `Image` that fires `onload` on `src`, an immediately-intersecting `IntersectionObserver` and a capped `requestAnimationFrame` (the draw functions reschedule themselves, so an unconditional synchronous call would recurse forever) — which took `short-video-canvas.tsx` to **84.9%** (mounting every template id, each a separate `draw` branch, plus the mouse and touch drag handlers) and `dynamic-cover-canvas.tsx` to **96.6%** (both the phone and desktop layouts, under two measured boxes); `src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx` (**100%**) drives password sign-in, the MFA challenge and its back/verify, OAuth and every refusal; and the two largest, `src/app/(main)/feed/page.tsx` (**56.2%**) and `src/app/(main)/profile/page.tsx` (**71.4%**), drive the composer's optimistic publish and its rollback, pagination, refresh, every tab, the message dialog and the member list. The suite went from 1078 tests / 103 files to **1201 / 115**, and the whole-tree baseline rose from **72.97 / 70.5 / 52.32** to **84.46 / 74.9 / 63.81** lines/branches/functions. A follow-on pass then covered the handlers those two pages still left dead — deleting and editing an *owned* post on both the feed and the profile (the card only offers its options menu when the post's author is the viewer, so the fixture had to hold the reader's own posts), and the cover editor's Save / Remove cover / Remove video paths (the last two reachable only with a cover set on the profile the fixture returns). That took the feed page from 56.2 to **62.2%** lines (functions 10 → 75%) and the profile from 71.4 to **83.0%** (functions 13.3 → 63.3%), the suite to **1213 tests / 115 files**, and the whole-tree totals to **86.15 / 75.23 / 65.87**; the per-file floor still passes on all 168 files. One trap found doing it: `stubFetch` answers a bare value as JSON 200, so a `Response` handed to it as an *endpoint value* never carries its status — only a handler that returns a `Response` does, which the failure-path tests need and one initially did not.
- **A per-file floor now sits behind the directory aggregates, as a script rather than a Vitest threshold.** `coverage.thresholds.perFile` cannot express it: that flag is **global**, so turning it on applies per-file checking to *every* threshold set — the `src/lib/**` aggregate would silently become "every src/lib file ≥ 88%", which is not what that number means and would fail on files the aggregate exists to average. There is no per-glob `perFile`. So the floor lives in `.freebuff/coverage-floor.mjs`, and `test:coverage` is now `vitest run --coverage && npm run coverage:floor` — the report `.coverage/coverage-summary.json` is written by the run and every measured file is then checked on its own against **51% lines and statements**. Lines and statements together (the two measure the same execution in nearly every file). On top of that the **pure-logic directories are held on branches and functions too** — `src/lib/**` at **59 / 60** and `src/utils/**` at **99 / 99**, each a point or so under that directory's lowest file (`src/lib/db/ensure-profile.ts` 60.00% branches, `src/lib/r2.ts` 61.53% functions, and `src/utils` at 100 on both), because a pure unit's branch is a case a test should have made and its function is a unit a test should have called. `src/components/**` and `src/app/**` are deliberately *not* held on those metrics: a component's branch count is dominated by render conditionals and its value depends on how many states the test chose to mount, so a per-file number there would say more about testing style than about tests. Two files are exempt from the *extra* metrics because their number is structurally zero rather than a gap — `src/lib/db/schema.ts` (0/46: Drizzle table and column definitions, exercised as data at import, not called) and `src/utils/supabase/client.ts` (0/1: the browser-client factory every test replaces with a mock) — and both are still held to the base floor. It is a plain script and not a test on purpose: a test would read a report that only exists in the coverage run, so it would be absent — and silently skipped — under a plain `npm test`, whereas here a missing report is a loud failure. CI's **Test** job already runs `npm run test:coverage`, so it enforces both gates. Verified: the full run passes with `coverage-floor: 168 file(s) at or above 51% lines and statements; src/lib/** on branches 59% / functions 60%; src/utils/** on branches 99% / functions 99% (2 exemption(s)).`; against a crafted report, one `src/lib` file at 60/61 branches/functions passed while another at 58/59 failed both as `(directory floor)`, and the two exempt files passed at 0 — so both the extra floors and the exemptions are load-bearing; `node .freebuff/coverage-floor.mjs --threshold 99` fires on 156 metrics (`51.39% lines src/components/social/post-card.tsx` first), so the comparison is load-bearing rather than a constant `true`; and a missing report exits 1 with a message naming `npm run test:coverage`. **The floor was then raised from 50 to 51**, which is as high as the current tree allows with any headroom: the binding file is `src/components/social/post-card.tsx` at **51.39% lines/statements** (not one of the twelve above), so 51 leaves 0.39 of margin — deliberately thin, and the reason to cover that file before pushing the floor higher. The raise was shown to be load-bearing rather than cosmetic: against a crafted report holding one file at 50.50% and one at 51.50%, the 51 floor failed on exactly the 50.50% file and left the 51.50% one alone — a check the old 50 floor could not have made.
- **The coverage numbers are now published on every run, not merely gated, so the ratchet has a trajectory rather than only a tripwire.** A green run and a run that cleared every threshold by a tenth of a point look identical in a log, and the question the gates cannot answer is *how much room is left*. `.freebuff/coverage-report.mjs` (`npm run coverage:report`) reads the same `.coverage/coverage-summary.json` the floor reads and renders: the whole-tree totals, one aggregate row per glob **next to the threshold that row is held to** (so every cell is `84.46% (+12.46)`, and a margin under one point is marked ⚠ because that is where a shared checkout turns a neighbour's untested line into a red build), a row for the files no glob names, and the weakest files — which are what caps the per-file floor and therefore what to cover next. In CI it is a step with **`if: always()`**, so a failing gate still publishes; it appends the markdown to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (the job's own summary page) and writes `.coverage/coverage-report.md`, and the workflow uploads that plus the raw `coverage-summary.json` as a **`coverage-report` artifact kept 30 days** — which is how a commit is diffed against another: download two summaries and run `node .freebuff/coverage-report.mjs --compare <older>` for a Δ-lines column. **The thresholds themselves moved out of `vitest.config.ts` into `.freebuff/coverage-thresholds.mjs`**, which is the one source of truth now: the config enforces them and the report reads them, so the headroom column cannot claim slack the gate does not have. That move is behavior-preserving — a deliberate small run (`vitest run src/test/runbook-contents.test.ts --coverage`) still fails against the same numbers, now sourced from the module (`Coverage for lines (0%) does not meet "src/lib/**" threshold (88%)`, global backstop 72, and so on). Verified: against the real report the table reads 168 files at **86.15 / 75.23 / 65.88** lines/branches/functions, with `src/lib/**` 27 files at 93.64/88.11/69.23, `src/utils/**` 3 at 98.55/100/85.71, `src/app/**` 59 at 84.79/71.95/70.00, `src/components/**` 74 at 85.89/75.00/59.16, and the two no-glob files (`src/index.ts`, `src/middleware.ts`) at 100 — and `src/hooks/**` is the tight row at **77.43% vs its 77% floor (+0.43)**; the weakest files are `authenticator-security.tsx` 52.87, `post-card.tsx` 53.38, `record-cover-video.ts` 54.54. `--compare` was proven on a crafted older summary (whole tree scaled to 90%, every `src/hooks` file halved): the Δ column read `+8.61` for the tree and `+38.87` for `src/hooks/**`, `+0.00` for the untouched directories. A missing report exits 1 naming `npm run test:coverage`. **What this makes visible:** the bare backstop was still 72/72/69/51, well under the tree's then-current 86.15 / 75.23 / 65.88, and the per-file floor was still 51 while the weakest file was `authenticator-security.tsx` at **52.87%** — both could be raised, and the report was what showed by how much; the next bullet is that raise.
- **The thresholds and the per-file floor were raised to match what the report publishes, closing the slack at both ends.** The raise is against the live numbers, not the snapshot above: the full run at this writing reads 168 files at **86.26 / 75.57 / 65.88** lines/branches/functions, with `src/lib/**` 27 files at 93.64/87.58/69.23, `src/utils/**` 3 at 98.55/100/85.71, `src/hooks/**` 3 at 77.43/73.33/71.43, `src/app/**` 59 at 85.03/72.74/70.00, and `src/components/**` 74 at 85.89/75.00/59.16. The bare backstop moved from **72/72/69/51 to 85/85/74/64**; `src/lib/**` from 88/88/86/58 to **92/92/86/67**; `src/app/**` from 77/77/68/57 to **83/83/70/68**; `src/components/**` from 63/63/63/41 to **84/84/73/57**. Each now sits 1.2–2.7 points under its measured aggregate, so a real regression trips it and a rounding wobble does not. Three rows were deliberately *not* moved because they have no slack left: `src/hooks/**` (77/77/73/71, every metric under half a point over today's number) and `src/utils/**` (98/98/99/85), and `src/lib/**`'s **branches** stayed at 86 rather than rising to 87 — the two full runs that bracketed this pass read 88.11 and then 87.58 on that one metric, so anything above 86 would flag slack the gate does not actually have. **The per-file floor went from 51% to 52%**, which is as high as the tree allows: the binding file is now `src/components/auth/authenticator-security.tsx` at **52.87%** lines/statements (the floor script's own doc comment had named `post-card.tsx` at 51.39 as binding, long since passed, and was corrected), so 52 leaves 0.87 of margin. The raise is load-bearing, shown two ways: a small run (`vitest run src/test/runbook-contents.test.ts --coverage`) fails with the *new* numbers in every message — `Coverage for lines (0%) does not meet global threshold (85%)`, `... "src/lib/**" threshold (92%)`, `... "src/hooks/**" threshold (77%)`, `... "src/app/**" threshold (83%)`, `... "src/components/**" threshold (84%)` — proving the config reads the raised module rather than the old one; and against a crafted report holding one file at 51.50% and one at 52.00%, the 52 floor fails on exactly the 51.50% file and leaves the 52.00% one alone, a check the old 51 floor could not have made. The full `npm run test:coverage` is green (115 files / 1220 tests, floor passing on all 168 files), as are `npm run lint:ci` and `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- **The last two tight rows were raised by covering the files that capped them, starting with `src/hooks/use-presence.ts`.** `use-presence.ts` (56.96% lines, 50% branches) got `src/hooks/use-presence.test.tsx`: the hook is mounted through a harness with `@/hooks/use-websocket` mocked, so a test delivers online/offline messages by re-rendering and reads the answer — the map before any message, a user marked online, the last-seen time kept across a going-offline, the non-string-id guards on both cases, an unrelated message type, all three `formatLastSeen` buckets on a `Date.now` spy, `checkPresence`'s send, and the passthrough `isConnected`. **100% on every metric.** The other capping file, `src/hooks/use-websocket.ts` (74.12% lines, 60% branches/functions), got `src/hooks/use-websocket.test.tsx`: the browser's `WebSocket` is replaced with a fake the test drives (`open`/`deliver`/`close`/`fail`), `useSession` is stubbed, and the coverage is the URL built from the user and room (both `ws://` and `wss://`), the no-session no-op plus the `connect` guard driven directly, every named send serialized to JSON, the heartbeat, an incoming message and its unparseable counterpart, a socket error, the reconnect ladder up to `maxReconnectAttempts` and its stop, and manual `disconnect` cancelling a pending reconnect — **100% lines/functions**, the one branch it left being nothing (the last was reached by calling `connect` directly). The utils row was capped by the browser Supabase factory: `src/utils/supabase/client.ts` was 0/1 functions and exempt from the utils function floor; `src/utils/supabase/client.test.ts` sets the two env vars through `vi.hoisted` (the module reads them at import, so assigning after would test values it never saw), mocks `@supabase/ssr`, and asserts the factory forwards both credentials — **100% lines/functions**. Aggregates: `src/hooks/**` **77.43/73.33/71.43 → 99.69/94.85/100**, `src/utils/**` **98.55/100/85.71 → 100/100/100**. Thresholds moved with them: hooks **77/77/73/71 → 98/98/93/99** (`lines` cannot go to 99 because `use-file-upload.ts` is 98.96, and `branches` sits under the row's 94.85) and utils **98/98/99/85 → 99/99/99/99**. The per-file floor's utils **functions/branches 99/99** now reach the browser factory too — its exemption was removed, since it has a unit of its own now, so the success line reads `(1 exemption(s))`. Load-bearing, shown two ways: a small run (`vitest run src/test/runbook-contents.test.ts --coverage`) fails with the *new* numbers — `"src/hooks/**" threshold (98%)`, `"src/utils/**" threshold (99%)` — proving the config reads the raised module; and against a crafted report the factory at 50% functions now fails as `(directory floor)` while at 100% it passes, a check the old exemption could not make. Two things learned doing it: **`disconnect()` closes the socket, the fake's `close()` fires `onclose`, and the hook answers a close with a reconnect** — on real timers that lands in the *next* test as a socket nobody opened, so the file runs on fake timers throughout; and the shared checkout's full-run coverage was unreliable at this moment (another session running the suite collapsed per-file line totals to `1/1` and rewrote `.coverage`), so the aggregate moved here was measured from a targeted `npx vitest run src/hooks src/utils --coverage` run — 6 files / 38 tests — which is deterministic for those files.
- **The whole-tree backstop now has a margin gate, so the ratchet tightens without anyone editing a number.** `.freebuff/coverage-headroom.mjs` (`npm run coverage:headroom`) reads the same `.coverage/coverage-summary.json` the floor and the report read, computes the whole-tree aggregate exactly as the report's first row does (`summary.total` when the reporter supplies it, otherwise the per-file counts summed), and **fails when it clears any bare backstop by less than a point** — so with the backstop at 85/85/74/64 the effective enforcement line is 86/86/75/65, and it rises on its own as the tree improves while the thresholds file stays where it is. The boundary is inclusive and matches the report's `⚠`: exactly `+1.00` passes, `+0.99` does not. `test:coverage` is now `vitest run --coverage && npm run coverage:floor && npm run coverage:headroom`, so the gate runs in CI's **Test** job where the floor already does (the workflow comment now names all three), and the report's `if: always()` step is unchanged — a gate failure still publishes the numbers, because that is the run worth reading. **Every `⚠` on the whole-tree row of the report is therefore a red build**, and both the report's header and its `cell()` comment say so. It is a plain script rather than a Vitest threshold for the same reason the floor is: Vitest checks the bare numbers against the whole tree only, and nothing expresses "the aggregate must also clear them by a point". The comment is gated on `earned`: a row *this* change actually moved against the baseline. Slack that was already there is still listed and labelled (`N of them are slack this change did not create`), because hiding it would defeat publishing the proposal, but a PR that touched no coverage gets no comment.
