`npm run runbook:check` is up to date (60 sections).
## Reading a group's members is now the group admin's alone
- **The three sweeps' survivor vocabularies are one module now, so a fourth sweep inherits the refusal and the spelling pins by importing it.** `STRIKE_WORDS`, both sweeps' `SURVIVOR_WORDS` tables and the coverage launcher's `SURVIVOR_WHY` lived beside the sweep that read them, which meant the two-way refusal was re-declared per sweep and a new sweep copied the pattern by hand — copies that could then drift one from another, with nothing saying they had. The fix is `.freebuff/mutation-vocabulary.mjs`: the tables are declared once there (`PREFLIGHT_SURVIVOR_WORDS` / `COVERAGE_SURVIVOR_WORDS`, imported under the local name each report already speaks, so every refusal sentence keeps its spelling), with `vocabularyHoles` — the both-ways stamps-versus-declared comparison the refusals act on — as the one function, because it is one contract. What stays in each sweep on purpose: its stamp scan (what counts as a stamp is that sweep's own shape — a `kind:` literal, a `KIND_*` constant, an entry resolved through `strikeKind`) and its refusal (a survivor object shaped to its payload). Moving the guards' table exposed a shape the copies had hidden: its refusal reads *entries* where the other two read bare kinds, so the shared comparison answers in stamps and the guards' `vocabularyAbsences` maps the unnamed kinds back to the strikes that stamp them — the refusal names the entry, not a bare word, exactly as before. **Held by a suite:** the spelling pins re-point at the module (the guards' families case, the preflight/coverage copy-splice refusal cases, the runner's stage-vocabulary describe and its scan-health probes, the launcher's `SURVIVOR_WHY` spells-once case), and a new case in the runner's suite finds every consumer by its import shape, so a sweep that stops reading the shared module reds instead of silently leaving its refusal behind; a fourth sweep that imports `./mutation-vocabulary.mjs` under `as SURVIVOR_WORDS` (or `STRIKE_WORDS`) is discovered by that case and held without a new test. The CI runner's stage cache keys fold the module in through the import closure and the drift alarm already watched `mutation-*.mjs`, so both sides picked it up without an edit. **Proven load-bearing by hand, margin one, restored byte-exact (`cmp`, `sha1sum` `253c6204…`):** renaming a mark's *value* in the module reds the runner's exact-value hold ("the coverage stage rewords `survived`") and the report-heading spelling pin while the refusal cases stay green — correct, since a value rename is no hole; renaming a table *key* reds that sweep's stamp probe ("declares `outlived` but no longer stamps it") and the stage key hold, nothing else. The copy mechanics were proven the hard way: the suites' sibling copies re-point their import at a per-suite copy of the module (spliced when a case declares a word the table must lack), and a first cut that gave every suite one shared copy file raced between workers — a copy ran the real table and the case passed vacuously until the runs were read together. **Readings.** `node --check` clean on all three sweeps and the module, `npx eslint` clean on the four suites, `npx tsc --noEmit` 0; a real coverage pass on the new module reads 5 checked, no survivors; the five targeted suites read **233 passed | 1 skipped**; pins `.freebuff/mutation-guards.mjs` `7715d0df → 2820334e`, `.freebuff/mutation-preflight.mjs` `c5a62118 → ff3d22cb`, `.freebuff/mutation-coverage.mjs` `7a2c105b → 04bc24eb`, `.freebuff/mutation-vocabulary.mjs` pinned new; `node .freebuff/gate-drift.mjs --status` reads 45 pinned, all match; `npm run runbook:check` is up to date (60 sections).

- **The first finding worth recording is that a group has no company and no Page, so "company-admin" cannot be applied to it literally.** `groups` carries only `{id, name, description, categoryId, coverUrl, visibility, createdAt}` — there is no `page_id` to defer to and no `companies` row pointing back. The only admin a group has is the `role` column on its own `group_members` row (`role` default `"member"`, admin when `"admin"`), which `POST` already reads for its last-admin rule. The company-admin model from `jobs`/`marketplace` (admin of the Page a company belongs to) simply does not exist here, so this pass gates on the edge that does.
- **The route had no `GET` at all, so the gated `GET` is new; `POST` is untouched because it is a self-service join/leave toggle.** `src/components/groups/group-card.tsx` and `src/app/(main)/groups/[id]/page.tsx` call it with only `{groupId}` to join or leave, and the route only ever writes the session user's own row — a company-admin gate on `POST` would break joining and leaving for exactly the people it is for. That is why the request's "non-admin `403`" is pinned on the read (whose answer *is* other people's membership data) rather than on the toggle (whose write is already the caller's own). Decided with the user before implementing.
- **The route's `md5` has changed** (`10a86e3ff893620b9c86ebe2401aaa4c` → `51f50a6d057bca6b00eef6eec931dcd4`). `GET` reads `groupId` from the query (missing → `400 Group ID is required`, reading nothing), reads the group (`404 Group not found` when it is not there), reads the caller's own `group_members` row and refuses a caller whose role is not `admin` with `403 Only a group admin can view members` — **before** the member rows are read — and only then reads the members. `POST` keeps its whole shape: `400` without a `groupId`, `404` without the group, the last admin of a group leaving a `409 Add another admin before leaving this community`, an existing row deleted → `{member:false}`, otherwise the caller inserted as a `member` → `{member:true}` with `201`.

## A `failNextSelect` seam, and the read-failure branches it pins

- **The harness could script a failed write but not a failed read, so every route's read-failure branch was untestable.** `FakeDb` had `failNextUpdate`/`failNextInsert`; a `select` could only ever be answered with rows. `failNextSelect(table, error?)` closes the gap (`src/test/fake-db.ts` `ad103787e4d47cd665ca9f67605bf04d`): a queued error makes the next `select` of that table reject when it is awaited, exactly as a dropped connection would. Like the write seams, a rejected read is **not** recorded in `reads` — the route asked and got no answer, the same line the write seams draw — and the queue is per table, cleared by `resetFakeDb()`.
- **Thirteen read-failure tests now exercise it, none of them possible before.** The branch each pins: `preferences` `GET` `503` (the one the route's own comment calls "an honest failure rather than an invented empty preference"); `users` `GET` and `PUT` falling back to `200 persistence: "auth-metadata"`; `users/block` `POST` `500`; `users/brief` `GET` `500`; `users/follow` `GET` `500` **and** `POST` `500`; `search` `GET` `500`; `notifications` `GET` `500` and `POST` `500`; `pages/follow` `POST` `500`; `posts/counts` `GET` `500`; `posts/reports` `POST` `500`. Most also assert no write followed — a failed read must not turn into a partial write.
- **The other half of the audit: routes that read under a `catch` but never drove the seam.** Walking every `route.ts` with a neighbour test for `select` + `catch` against whether the test mentions `failNextSelect` found **fourteen** files that never drove it. Five have no `GET` at all (their reads live inside write handlers), and `profile/avatar` and `auth/callback` already drive the catch through a write seam (`failNextUpdate`/`failNextInsert`), so their `500` is not dead. The **GET read-failure branches were all dead**, and each now has a test: `groups/members`, `jobs`, `jobs/applications`, `marketplace`, `marketplace/inventory`, `pages`, `posts`, `posts/comments`, `posts/reactions`. Four of those files (`jobs`, `marketplace`, `pages`, `posts`) did not even import `GET` — their whole GET handler was untested, so the new test is the first to call it. Each fails the handler's *first* read and asserts the `500`, its message, and `expectGatedNone("reads")` — a rejected read is not recorded. The remaining reads that sit inside a write handler's `catch` are catalogued but not yet driven.
- **The `notifications` `POST` test is the subtle one.** Its `POST` performs an `update` and *then* a recount `select`, so `updateReturns` supplies the updated rows and `failNextSelect` fails the recount: the test pins that a failure *after* a successful write still answers `500` rather than a half-truth.
- **The seam is verified load-bearing, not just present.** Three mutations, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified: changing the `preferences` `GET` failure from `503` to `500` failed **exactly 1** (its read-failure test); changing the `users/follow` `GET` failure from `500` to `200` failed **exactly 1**; and — the one that proves the *seam* rather than a route — making `takeSelect` swallow the queued error (`if (error) void error`) failed **exactly 1** (the `preferences` `503` test, which then saw a `200`). A seam nothing depends on is dead code; this check is what says this one is not.
- **One avoidable stumble:** the first `search` read-failure test failed with `ReferenceError: users is not defined` because the search test file did not import the schema object, only `fakeDb`. Fixed by importing `users` from `@/lib/db/schema`.
- **Totals after this pass:** `npm test -- --run` reads **791 passed / 75 files** (the thirteen new tests); `npm run build` completed; `npx tsc --noEmit` reads **0**. Read every count as a property of the checkout at that moment.

## Blocks are enforced, in both directions

- **The audit's first critical finding was that a block was written and never read.** `POST /api/users/block` inserted into `blocks`, but nothing else in `src/app` consulted the table: a blocked member could still message, follow, and appear in the member list and search results of the person who blocked them. This pass adds the one shared rule and consults it at every meeting point.
- **`src/lib/db/blocks.ts` is new, and holds a single rule in the two shapes callers need.** `blockedEitherWay(a, b)` is a condition on `blocks` — `(blocker=a and blocked=b) or (blocker=b and blocked=a)` — with `a` and `b` each a bound id or a column of the surrounding query, so a write can ask it for one pair and a read can negate it per row. `notBlockedEitherWay(viewerId, candidate)` wraps that same predicate in a correlated `not exists` for a list query. Both are qualified, and `blocks.test.ts` renders them through the query builder: the second direction is what a one-way check would miss, and the correlation has to run outward (an unqualified `blocked_id` inside the subquery would compare the block to itself).
- **Every meeting point now consults it.** `POST /api/messages` refuses a recipient a block stands between with `403 You cannot message this member` before any read of conversations or any write (and rejects a non-uuid recipient `400`, since the id is bound into the block lookup). `POST /api/users/follow` refuses `403 You cannot follow this member` after the target-exists `404` and before any follow write. `GET /api/users/follow` and the member arm of `GET /api/search` carry `notBlockedEitherWay(viewer, users.id)` in their `where`, so a blocked member is dropped from the list in either direction. Routes changed: `src/app/api/messages/route.ts` `04f3f6fd346b4daefb663956539d4702`, `src/app/api/users/follow/route.ts` `d3506437f428b24d300dfe05b20e7dcd`, `src/app/api/search/route.ts` `a84ebb52ef1d5341da8f5aa4f32e220f`.
- **The fake gained a read-`where` capture, because it cannot evaluate a predicate.** `FakeDb` records only the table a chain started from, so a route filtering a list with `not exists` looked identical to one that did not filter at all. It now renders each select's `where` with `PgDialect` into `selectWheres` (aligned with `reads`, `""` when unfiltered) — the condition is still not evaluated, but the test can now pin that a list is *gated*. That is what the two list-read tests assert (`not exists`, `from "blocks"`, and the outer correlation). Harness: `src/test/fake-db.ts` `a9f4fd3a90f3f22b8a71d958491212a2`.
- **`src/app/api/messages/route.test.ts` (12 tests) is new, and covers both methods.** `GET`: `401` before any read; the conversation list; `404` for a conversation that is not there; `403` when the caller is not a member; and the single-conversation read pinned as the read order (`conversations` → `conversation_members` → `messages` → `conversation_members`) with the `lastReadAt` write recorded. `POST`: `401`; `400` with no reads for missing recipient/content; `400` for a non-uuid recipient; `403` with nothing written (not even an empty conversation) when a block row comes back; a new conversation created with the three writes in order; a send into the existing conversation with only the `messages` write; and a `500` when the block lookup fails. `src/app/api/users/follow/route.test.ts` grew to **23 tests** (the `403` refusal, a follow that still proceeds when the block read is empty, a `500` on the block read, and the `GET` predicate pin); `src/app/api/search/route.test.ts` to **7** (the member-arm predicate pin); `src/lib/db/blocks.test.ts` is **4** new tests.
- **Mutations, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified** (`blocks.ts` `472e9f3b267ff9b97d223e04b0edfb8c`): dropping the second direction from the rule failed **exactly 3** (the two `blockedEitherWay` tests and the `notBlockedEitherWay` correlation test); removing the `users/follow` `POST` block guard failed **exactly 2** (the `403` test, and the read-failure test whose `writes: []` assertion then caught the stray insert); removing the `messages` `POST` block guard failed **exactly 2** (the same pair); removing the `GET` list predicate failed **exactly 1**; and removing the search predicate failed **exactly 1**.
- **The coverage ratchet was updated with it:** `/api/messages` was removed from `UNTESTED_API`, leaving the `admin/moderate`, `admin/reports` and the `auth` pair as the only entries.
- **Totals after this pass:** `npm test -- --run` reads **813 passed / 77 files**; `npm run build` completed; `npx tsc --noEmit` reads **0**. Read every count as a property of the checkout at that moment.

## Comment and reaction reads are gated by the post's audience

- **The audit's third critical finding was that a post's thread and counters bypassed its audience.** `GET /api/posts/comments` had no reference to `posts` at all: `?postId=` returned any post's comments and `?ids=` hydrated any comment by id, so a `private`, `followers` or `group` post's conversation was readable by naming it. `GET /api/posts/reactions` was the same shape for reaction counts. Both reads now consult the same `visiblePostsCondition` every other post read already uses. Writes are untouched — the request was the reads.
- **`src/app/api/posts/comments/route.ts` (`63cbbd7a042ae8e0e0f1e1316595a37c`) gates its two paths differently, on purpose.** The `?postId=` path first reads the post with the predicate and answers `404 Post not found` when it is not there or not visible, so a thread is only served for a post the viewer may read (a missing post and an invisible one are the same non-answer). The `?ids=` path, which hydrates comments across an open feed, joins `posts` on the comment's `post_id` and adds the predicate to its `where`, so a comment on an invisible post is simply not returned. The `session` that `requireAuth` already returned is now used rather than discarded.
- **`src/app/api/posts/reactions/route.ts` (`d4aca533182440f5d9fbfb4ed1658092`) gates on the target.** For `targetType=post` it reads the post with the predicate and answers `404` when it is not visible, before the reaction rows are read; any other target type is read directly, since only a post carries an audience (pinned by a `targetType=comment` case that reads only `reactions`).
- **The neighbour tests grew rather than being rewritten:** `src/app/api/posts/comments/route.test.ts` and `src/app/api/posts/reactions/route.test.ts` are now **8 tests each** (from 6). The existing happy-path `GET` tests script the new `posts` read in front, and each file gains an invisible-post `404` case plus a pin on the guard's `where` (via `selectWheres`), asserting the read carries the audience rule (`"visibility" = 'public'` and an `exists`) rather than merely touching the table.
- **Mutations, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified.** Removing the comments `?postId=` guard failed **exactly 2** (the `404` test and the envelope test, whose read-order and predicate pins then caught the missing post read); removing the `?ids=` predicate failed **exactly 1**; and removing the reactions post guard failed **exactly 2** (the `404` test and the counts test, for the same two reasons).
- **Coverage ratchet unaffected** — no new route files, and both routes already had neighbour tests.
- **Totals after this pass:** `npm test -- --run` reads **817 passed / 77 files**; `npm run build` completed; `npx tsc --noEmit` reads **0**. Read every count as a property of the checkout at that moment.

## Media processing is confined to the caller's own storage folder

- **The audit's second critical finding was that `POST /api/media/process` trusted a `key` from the body.** It fetched whatever R2 object the key named and wrote `…-thumbnail.webp`, `…-small.webp` and so on beside it, with no ownership check — so any signed-in member could read any object by guessing a key, and write derived assets into another member's prefix. The route now requires the key to be under the caller's own folder before storage is touched (`src/app/api/media/process/route.ts` `f4e6b85d4ef696805921ddbd59a24d25`). It also refuses a non-string key with `400`, which the old `if (!key)` let through to a thrown `key.split`.
- **The rule lives next to the key generator, in `src/lib/r2.ts` (`86ad4ae081b36c1519124799bbd611e3`), because the key format is that module's.** `keyBelongsToUser(key, userId)` accepts a key whose second path segment is exactly the member id — the `<folder>/<userId>/<file>` shape `generateKey` has always produced — and refuses a key under anybody else's folder, a key too short to hold a member segment, and a traversal (`posts/../member-1/…`, whose second segment is `..`). Matching the whole segment rather than a prefix matters: `member-10` begins `member-1`, so `startsWith` would let one member process another's uploads.
- **No in-app caller uses this route**, so requiring the caller's own folder is safe to tighten; the pages-image path that stores keys under a Page id is a different route, and `/api/media/process` is not part of it.
- **Tests:** `src/lib/r2.test.ts` grew **+5** cases for `keyBelongsToUser` (own folder under several folders, another member, the `member-10` prefix lookalike, too-short keys, and the id appearing at the wrong segment); `src/app/api/media/process/route.test.ts` grew **+3** (a `403` for another member's key asserting the object is never fetched, config never asserted and nothing derived; a `403` for short and traversal keys; and a `400` for a non-string key). The route tests keep the real key helper because they mock `@/lib/r2` with `...actual`.
- **Mutations, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified.** Removing the route's ownership guard failed **exactly 2** (the other-member and short-key refusals); changing the helper's exact segment compare to `startsWith` failed **exactly 1** (the prefix-lookalike test).
- **Coverage ratchet unaffected** — no new route files, and the route already had a neighbour test.

## Moderating a report is validated, gated on `pending`, and cannot escape its `try`

- **The audit's medium finding was that `POST /api/admin/moderate` took the client at its word on three things.** The `action` it wrote was never checked against the enum column it lands in, a report that was already closed could be resolved a second time (stacking another `moderation_actions` row and audit row over the first), and the admin/moderator role read sat *before* the `try` — so a database error on that one lookup rejected out of the handler as an uncaught `500` instead of the route's own error answer. `src/app/api/admin/moderate/route.ts` (`a1676fe6017dad7bbb1f8497171c9238`) fixes all three.
- **The role check moved inside the `try` unchanged.** A caller who is not an admin or moderator is still `403 Unauthorized`, but a failure of that lookup is now the route's `500 Failed to moderate` — authorization must not answer "allowed" on error, and a handler that throws before its own error boundary has no answer at all.
- **The action is validated against `moderationActionEnum.enumValues` (`warning`, `removal`, `suspension`, `ban`) with `400 Invalid moderation action`, before the report is even read** — so an unknown action is a bad request rather than a constraint violation at write time.
- **A report is only resolved while `pending`; anything else is `409 Report is not pending`, read before any write.** No moderation action, no `resolved` update and no audit row are made over a report that already had a decision.
- **`src/app/api/admin/moderate/route.test.ts` (9 tests) is new** and drives the handler through the fake DB: `401` before any read; `403` for a non-admin (the role read only, nothing written); **`500` when the role read fails — which is exactly the uncaught-throw the old ordering produced**; `400` for a missing id/action and for an unknown action (both reading no report); `404` for a missing report; `409` for a non-pending report asserting nothing was written; a `201` asserting the three writes in order (the action carrying the report's target and the session actor, the `resolved` status, and the audit row under `moderation.`); and a `201` for a `moderator`, not only an `admin`.
- **Mutations, each reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified.** Removing the action validation failed **exactly 1** (the unknown-action test); removing the `pending` check failed **exactly 1** (the `409` test); and moving the role read back above the `try` failed **exactly 1** (the `500`-on-role-read-failure test, whose `await` rejects when the handler throws).
- **The coverage ratchet moved with it:** `/api/admin/moderate` was removed from `UNTESTED_API`, leaving `admin/reports` and the `auth` pair as the only entries.
- **Totals after this pass:** `npm test -- --run` reads **835 passed / 78 files**; `npm run build` completed; `npx tsc --noEmit` reads **0**. Read every count as a property of the checkout at that moment.

## A malformed block target is a 400, not a database type error

- **The audit's low finding was that `POST /api/users/block` bound the body's `userId` straight into the block lookup.** A signed-in caller could send a non-uuid — `"not-a-uuid"`, a number, an object — and the `blocks` query would raise a type error that surfaced as `500 Failed to toggle block`. The route now checks the id with `isUuid` (`src/app/api/users/block/route.ts` `634882e7f53125aa20923d6cedc6fefb`) and answers `400 Invalid user ID`.
- **The guard sits after the self-check, on purpose.** A real session id is always a uuid, so `userId === session.user.id` implies a well-formed id; keeping the self-check first means an attempt to block yourself still answers `Cannot block yourself` rather than `Invalid user ID`, and the malformed check only ever sees a target destined for the lookup. `typeof userId !== "string"` closes the non-string escape (`isUuid` would coerce).
- **`src/app/api/users/block/route.test.ts` (`947e849550eba0cd72fc5654e1a3d71c`) grew to 7 tests** with a malformed-target case that drives four shapes (`"not-a-uuid"`, a number, an object, and a truncated uuid) and asserts the `400 Invalid user ID` body with nothing read.
- **Mutation, reverted by hand and `md5sum -c`-verified.** Removing the `isUuid` guard failed **exactly 1** (the malformed-target test).
- **Totals after this pass:** `npm test -- --run` reads **837 passed / 78 files**; `npm run build` completed; `npx tsc --noEmit` reads **0**. Read every count as a property of the checkout at that moment.

## A malformed id is a 400 across the post, page, group, job, marketplace, comment and reaction routes

- **The block-target fix was the first of its class, and the class is every route that binds a caller-supplied id into a query.** A client could send a non-uuid — `"not-a-uuid"`, a number, an object — where the route expected a uuid, and Postgres would raise a type error that surfaced as the route's generic `500`. The pattern the `users/block` section established is now applied across the write *and* read handlers of the post, page, group, job, marketplace, comment and reaction routes: a malformed id is a `400` with the route's own message, answered **before** anything is read or written, so the bad input never reaches the column and no error path is dressed as an internal failure.
- **The predicate is `isUuid` from `src/lib/cursor-pagination.ts`**, imported as `import { isUuid } from "@/lib/cursor-pagination"`. Two spellings are used deliberately: `typeof id !== "string" || !isUuid(id)` where the value could be a non-string (`isUuid` would coerce, so the `typeof` closes that escape), and a bare `!isUuid(id)` where the value is already known to be a string. Each guard sits **after** its presence check (`if (!id) return … "… ID is required"`) and **before** the first database call, so a missing id and a malformed id stay distinct answers rather than collapsing into one.
- **The roster, by route (messages in quotes are the exact bodies):**
  - `posts/route.ts` — the list filters each reject a malformed value (`authorId`, `pageId`, `groupId` → `400 Invalid group id`, and any of `requestedIds`), and both writes carry `Invalid post id` (`:355` `DELETE`, `:405` `PUT`) behind their `Post ID is required` presence arms.
  - `pages/route.ts` — `Invalid page id` on the read (`:75`), `PUT` (`:222`) and `DELETE` (`:330`), plus `Invalid category id` on both writes.
  - `groups/route.ts` — `Invalid group ID` on the read (`:15`), `PUT` (`:159`) and `DELETE` (`:210`), plus `Invalid category id` on the writes.
  - `jobs/route.ts` — `Invalid job id` on the read (`:37`), `PUT` (`:230`) and `DELETE` (`:291`), plus `Invalid company id`.
  - `jobs/applications/route.ts` — `Invalid job id` on the read (`:67`) and the create (`:125`), and the id-shape check on the status `PUT` (`:180`).
  - `marketplace/route.ts` — `Invalid listing id` on the read (`:31`), `PUT` (`:212`) and `DELETE` (`:262`), plus `Invalid seller id` and `Invalid category id`.
  - `posts/comments/route.ts` — `Invalid post id` on the read (`:39`) and the create (`:129`), and a malformed element of the `ids` lookup parameter.
  - `posts/reactions/route.ts` — the `targetId` shape is checked before the reaction is read (`:19`) and before the toggle (`:97`).
- **The neighbour tests now assert the message, not merely the status.** The reason these guards survived the earlier sweeps was *masking*, not an uncased branch: a sibling refusal answered the same `400`, so a test that only pinned the status kept passing while the guard was droppable. Each route's `route.test.ts` gained a malformed-id case that drives the non-uuid shape and asserts the route's **own** body, which is what turns a removal or a fail-open mutation into a test failure. `src/app/api/jobs/applications/route.test.ts` is the worked example: its three presence guards (`:62` `!jobId` on the read, `:121` on the create, `:177` `!id || !status` on the `PUT`) previously survived because the new shape guard answered the same `400` with `Invalid job id` / a different message; they are now pinned by `Job ID is required` and `Application ID and status are required`, and the full sweep reports them caught.
- **Mutation evidence: the full sweep (`npm run mutation:guards`) reports `Every guard was caught by its neighbour test` — 530 mutations, 0 survivors**, with each new `isUuid` guard caught in both its removal and fail-open forms (e.g. `posts/route.ts:404 if (!isUuid(id))`, `pages/route.ts:75`, `groups/route.ts:15`, `jobs/applications/route.ts:66/124`, `marketplace/route.ts:31`, `pages/image/route.ts:47`).
- **No new route files**, so the coverage ratchet is unaffected; the change is guards plus message-asserting cases in the existing neighbour tests.

Two of the copies are now *generated*: a marked line in the runner's own header and one in this runbook, written by `npm run stages:write` out of the declaration, so the count in the prose cannot be typed at all. The markers are the whole structural convention, and the rule is that a marker counts only as a line of its own (bar a block comment's `*` gutter): that is what lets the runner's own header be watched by its own audit without the two constants that spell the markers reading as a block that opens and closes on one line, and the text between the markers is compared with the gutter taken back off, so the header and this file hold the same line in their own margins. **`src/test/ci-stage-order.test.ts` (12 tests) holds it from both ends:** the table the audit reports must equal the `STAGES` names read out of the source rather than a second list kept in step by hand, the committed tree must be green with both generated lines equal to what a generator would write (read back through the markers by the test's own reader), and every drift is made on a throwaway copy through `CI_STAGE_ORDER_ROOT` — a hand-typed generated line, an unclosed block, a block that is gone, a watched file removed, a wrong count, a list out of order, an enumeration item renamed, an enumeration item dropped — then driven through a *run* as well, to prove the finding stops it before its first stage (`failed: []`) rather than printing an apology over a pass. **The audit is struck by the sweep now rather than only broken by hand:** `stageOrderFindings` joined `RUNNER_MUTATIONS` in `.freebuff/mutation-guards.mjs` — `runnerQuiet()` on its declaration line, returning an empty answer — so a runner that stopped comparing copies to the table is a survivor the `mutation` stage reports, not a silence; turning the refusal off (`if (false && orderDrift.length > 0)`) fails all seven drift cases (7 of 12); and the sweep itself — `node .freebuff/mutation-guards.mjs --file=ci --json` — reads `3 checked, 0 survivors` under `self-mutations: 48 (10 test helper, 35 convention detector, 3 runner check)`, the new strike caught by `src/test/ci-stage-order.test.ts`. That is precisely the shape the bullet above teaches the runner to name, and it is still not a claim about the code under test, so it is not allowed to fail a run. `makeScratchDir(prefix)` / `removeScratchDir(dir)` replace the pair: the removal uses Node's own linear backoff for exactly those errnos (`maxRetries: 10`, `retryDelay: 50` — under three seconds at worst, and only for a `recursive` removal), and one that still fails is *reported* through a `write` seam rather than thrown, the same "report the environment and get out of the way" shape `src/test/checkout-watch.ts` uses for a checkout moving under the suite. The three runner suites (`src/test/ci-runner.test.ts`, `src/test/ci-runner-tree-editing.test.ts`, `src/test/ci-stage-order.test.ts`) are converted, and `src/test/scratch.test.ts` (4 tests) pins creation, a nested removal, the idempotent quiet second call, and the give-up branch. **What the test deliberately does not arrange is the retry itself:** a lingering handle cannot be built portably — Node opens files with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, so an open handle does not block the delete on Windows, and POSIX never blocks it — and a path no retry can help reaches the same branch, which is the half that matters (the hook is never handed a throw).
